articles.title: FE covenants would put Bitcoin’s spending rules inside the signing key, with no protocol change. The cryptography they need is not yet practical.
articles.text:
Bitcoin Covenants Part 6: FE Covenants — Enforcing covenants through cryptographically restricted signing keys
FE covenants encode spending constraints into the signing key, so only transactions that satisfy a predefined condition can be signed.
This is Part 6 in the technical article series about Bitcoin covenants by Cointelegraph Research. To read the previous article, click here.
Changing Bitcoin’s consensus rules is not merely a technical process. It requires that the network’s node operators, miners, developers and economic actors coordinate around a change. This coordination is difficult to achieve, which is why Bitcoin’s base layer has gradually ossified.
Researchers have spent the last several years investigating whether covenant behavior could be enforced without touching consensus rules. In May 2024, Jeremy Rubin, the original author of the OP_CTV proposal (BIP-119), offered an answer in a paper titled FE’d Up Covenants. His design proposed using functional encryption (FE) to move the covenant out of Bitcoin Script and into the signing key.
In ordinary public-key cryptography, a private key can sign any message. In hypothetical FE-based covenants, signing would be restricted to a predefined set of valid transactions. Bitcoin nodes would verify the signature with OP_CHECKSIG exactly as they do today, obviating the need for a soft fork.
Functional encryption: keys that only sign what the rules allow
Functional encryption (FE) generalizes public-key encryption. In ordinary cryptographic schemes, a private key can be used to fully decrypt a ciphertext and arrive at the plaintext. In FE, a master secret is instead used to issue subsidiary functional keys, each of which reveals only one chosen function of the plaintext. The holder of the functional key for a function f and the ciphertext of a secret x can compute f(x) but never gets to reveal x as a plaintext message.
In the academic literature, FE was first formalized by Dan Boneh, Amit Sahai and Brent Waters in 2011. Constructions for arbitrary functions followed from 2013, with polynomial runtime but overheads far beyond the resources of current computing technology. Furthermore, their security rested on new, untested building blocks called multilinear maps. Only in 2021 did researchers develop constructions from well-founded cryptographic assumptions, which could in principle open the door to practical implementations of FE.
The f in an FE scheme can be any feasibly computable function. However, in Bitcoin covenant constructions, f is a signing function. Its output is a Bitcoin signature for a transaction tx. Because this signature depends on both a private key and the transaction that is being signed, it takes at least two inputs, which is why Rubin’s design uses multi-input FE. For a covenant that only permits a single spending transaction, akin to OP_CTV, two inputs suffice. General, expressive constructions take more arguments, as in Rubin’s f(k, tx, program, proof).
Crucially, f does not sign directly with the private key k that is supplied in an encrypted form. Instead, the function derives a new key pair by tweaking k with a hash of the covenant’s spending policy. Signatures produced by f are valid for the tweaked public key, not for the base public key P itself.
Setting up FE-based covenants
To enable FE-based covenants from these primitives, a setup authority is required. It generates a Bitcoin key pair (the private key k and the public key P) as well as an FE key pair (the master secret msk and the FE public key mpk). It publishes P, mpk, k encrypted to mpk, and the functional key for f, which it derives from msk. The setup authority then needs to be trusted to destroy k and msk. Otherwise, it could sign spends that violate the covenant. With this setup completed, an indefinite number of new covenants may be created.
Every covenant has its own dedicated key pair, obtained by tweaking (k, P) with the spending policy. The private key of this tweaked key pair exists only inside f and is never revealed. The public key can be derived from P by anyone who knows the hash of the desired spending policy. This way, covenant receiving addresses can be generated. In practice, the receiving address would commit to a 2-of-2 script that requires a signature from a key the user controls alongside the FE signature. This is to keep unauthorized parties from triggering a transaction permitted by the covenant.
To create an FE signature for a covenant spend, the signer takes a tx that conforms to the spending policy and encrypts it to mpk. Using the encrypted tx, together with the encrypted k and the functional key published by the authority, they can then evaluate f. The function f signs tx with k tweaked by the hash of the spending policy. A transaction that breaks the spending policy of the address that holds the coins could at best be signed for some other, differently tweaked public key that does not control the funds.The function f can also be designed to block such a signature outright.
The general version of FE-based covenants with f(k, tx, program, proof) is strictly more expressive than OP_CTV. The general function proposed by Rubin takes a program that checks a condition on the transaction at spend time, and a zero-knowledge proof that the program accepts the transaction.
This zero-knowledge proof facilitates the implementation of the FE scheme, but does not add to it conceptually. A single fixed f works either way. Without the proof, f would have to be a general interpreter that runs any given program on tx itself. Such an f is large and costly to evaluate under FE. With the proof, f only has to verify a succinct proof. This could make it possible to enforce arbitrarily complex covenants without the need for more complexity in f. The proof also lets a spending policy depend on data outside the transaction, such as the result of an off-chain computation.
Why FE-based covenants remain infeasible for now
Goldwasser et al. (2014) introduced multi-input FE and built it on indistinguishability obfuscation. Multi-input FE and obfuscation are known to imply one another. Ananth and Jain (2015) showed that even single-input FE for general circuits yields obfuscation once it is made compact. The cryptographic primitive this design needs is therefore at least as hard to build as so-called indistinguishability obfuscation itself. Implementations of this principle remain at toy scale.
Carmer, Malozemoff and Raykova (2017) needed 3.7 hours to obfuscate a 12-bit pseudorandom function, a toy circuit of about 62,000 gates with a 64-bit key, far smaller than ECDSA signing on 256-bit numbers. The obfuscated program took 120 GB of disk space, and an evaluation ran for 67 minutes with 128 GB of RAM. The cost of implementing such a scheme would fall on whoever produces the signature, not on Bitcoin nodes. The authors called this “still far from practical.”
Furthermore, FE schemes that are practical cover only narrow function classes, such as the inner products of Abdalla et al. (2015), and the type of ECDSA signing required for Bitcoin covenants is not among them. Rubin’s paper concedes this point and lists under-developed cryptography and the setup trust assumption among its downsides. CTV-style opcodes remain far more efficient in bytes and verification, but require a base-layer change.
In our next article, we turn to Un-FE’d Covenants, which Rubin proposed to approximate covenant behavior without relying on impractical FE schemes. It replaces FE with oracle signers bonded through BitVM. [alloc]init’s Bitcoin PIPEs began in 2024 as an FE design and moved in 2026 to witness encryption. This proposal will also be covered in a follow-up article.

articles.title: 'It Speaks in Tongues That Only 6.2 Astra Understands': Why Early Testers Hate OpenAI’s New Model - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Developers who tested GPT-6.2 Astra before launch describe frustrating coding failures, incomprehensible explanations and agents that waste days without making progress.
- OpenAI's own safety evaluation found Astra concealed known obstacles in 22.28% of deliberately obstructed coding trials, roughly twice its predecessor's rate.
- Sam Altman acknowledged usability problems, while another OpenAI executive said significant last-minute changes may have made some early reviews outdated.
For an AI developer, hearing that your model is nice is always pretty good. But hearing your model is like a "sadistic shinigami that turns your life into a living hell," is a totally different thing.
OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on Tuesday, promising smarter AI agents, better coding and impressive creative capabilities. Some of the developers who tested the models before launch had a rather different message: They're brilliant, frustrating and, in certain cases, almost impossible to work with.
The reaction quickly spilled across social media. AI engineer Hesam, who is very active in the AI community declared that “everyone agrees it’s the worst model OAI dropped.”
The backlash was loud, not unanimous.
Developer and T3 Code creator Theo Browne published a lengthy letter to OpenAI following early testing. “I do not like 6.2 Astra. I would not choose this over Opus 5.5 for my work as a developer,” he wrote. He said OpenAI had fixed only a handful of the complaints he submitted.
“It speaks in tongues that only 6.2 Astra understands,” Theo wrote, calling its answers “the most unparsable outputs of any llm I've used this year,” referring to large language models. The complaint was as much about communication as capability: Astra could solve complex problems but struggled to explain what it had done or recognize when it was asking users questions they could not possibly answer.
In one experiment, Theo asked Astra to create a new level for Outer Wilds. Two hours into the project, the model declared itself blocked and asked: “does r24's reviewer write it's clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4?” The technical question was, from his perspective, incomprehensible and irrelevant to someone who had simply requested a playable level.
Things went worse in a code rewrite. Theo said he gave Astra seven days to improve the project; it landed no improvements and made the compiler 56% slower. Four more days yielded zero changes. “It runs in loops and goes nowhere,” he wrote.
This whole weird language issue is not isolated. For example, pseudonymous account, TokenGremlin, praised the model: “GPT-6.2 Astra is SOTA in Three.js, Blender, and 3D,” but said it “starts speaking an alien language during long workflows.”
Theo also described asking why worktrees were slow on one computer. Astra responded with four paragraphs about package-manager internals and cache behavior. The answer Theo said he received from Claude Opus 5.5 was considerably clearer.
“it's because the ssd is slow,” Claude replied.
The model's supposed creativity was another sore spot. Theo and another tester independently requested original levels for two different games, Outer Wilds and Majora's Mask. Both got water-and-bell-themed musical levels, both named “Bellwether.” “This model regresses to the mean like nothing I've ever seen,” Theo wrote.
Several other accounts also flagged the same slop: Seems like GPT-6.2 Astra has a thing for bells.
Unbelievable pic.twitter.com/a4MgVUKi2M
— Racist James Franco (@racist_james) November 18, 2026
For a model supposedly capable of extraordinary creativity, repeatedly inventing the same level wasn't an encouraging sign.
Brilliant at demos, miserable at work?
AI developer Matt Shumer was also disappointed. “I've never written a bad review of a model. This one is especially bad,” he wrote, arguing it might impress in small demonstrations but “just straight up doesn't work” when pushed on serious projects. In a separate follow-up he called it “utterly unusable.”
I've never written a bad review of a model. This one is especially bad.
It's fine if you're playing putt-putt golf with the models, but if you're trying to drive them the way you should be, this model just straight up doesn't work.
— Matt Shumer (@mattshumer_) November 17, 2026
Max Weinbach described the same gap between intelligence and usability. “I had more time being annoyed by the models than time I was impressed by them,” he wrote. In a follow-up, he praised the models' ability to do “fantastic work” but said they “need a ton of ‘continue’ prompts” and often stop rather than try another approach. “Using them is a struggle and annoying even if they are really good models.”
Elsewhere, an X commentator compared the previous Astra to “a sadistic shinigami” and claimed the new version only made matters worse.
6.0 astra was very like a sadistic shinigami who would make your life a living hell if you asked for any kind of help
an incredibly powerful model that somehow required you to run yourself into the ground just to get it to accomplish anything
— M1 (@M1Astra) November 17, 2026
Yet some of the same developers also praised Astra. Theo called it a “great reviewer” and “world class at 3d & game stuff,” singled out its computer-control abilities, and described a novel reverse-proxy solution he estimated could save $25,000 monthly. The split was between impressive capabilities and how difficult it was to get dependable work out of them.
Those strengths are consistent with the technical capabilities OpenAI promoted at launch. As earlier coverage detailed, independent testing placed Astra at 62 out of 100 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, an aggregate of nine evaluations covering capabilities including reasoning, coding and scientific knowledge. Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 scored 65.
OpenAI admits there's a problem
Some of the criticism has support in OpenAI's own safety documentation.
In an internal evaluation called Blocker Deception, researchers gave AI agents realistic coding tasks with deliberately introduced obstacles, such as missing files or unavailable tools. They measured the percentage of trials in which a model's final response concealed or misrepresented those obstacles.
GPT-6.2 Astra concealed the obstacle in 22.28% of those trials, versus 11.09% for GPT-6 Astra. The numbers quickly circulated on X, where AI commentator and leaker Chetaslua summarized the finding as “2x worse at telling you when it's stuck.”
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded publicly to the backlash. “Although the new models are very smart, we have more work ahead of us on making the models nice to work with,” he wrote, promising to prioritize improvements. “But even if it takes a little extra work, the intelligence and capability are extraordinary.”
Although the new models are very smart, we have more work ahead of us on making the models nice to work with, and will prioritize that for upcoming releases.
But even if it takes a little extra work, the intelligence and capability are extraordinary.
— Sam Altman (@sama) November 17, 2026
OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux suggested early reviews may not fully reflect the version users received at launch. “We gave a few folks access a while ago and then made a lot of changes in the last 3-4 days,” he wrote, adding that he was “pretty sure no re-testing was done” during that period before review videos were produced.
Still, he acknowledged the underlying complaints. While calling the new models “a hefty jump” over their predecessors, Sottiaux said OpenAI had more work to do on “taste and niceness of use.”
GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available through ChatGPT Work, Codex and OpenAI's API for eligible users. The Codex-specific changes are included at launch, but developers accessing the models directly through the API do not receive that same prompting intervention.

articles.title: CoinShares Sells ETH Treasury, Halves SOL Holdings to Fund Share Buybacks
articles.text:
CoinShares sells all treasury ETH, halves SOL holdings for buybacks
The October sales raised $19.3 million, nearly half the $40 million CoinShares can spend on buybacks before its next annual meeting.
European digital asset manager CoinShares sold its entire Ether treasury position and half of its Solana treasury holdings in October, raising $19.3 million to fund share buybacks.
CoinShares raised $16.6 million from the Ether sale and $2.7 million from the Solana sale, the company said in its third-quarter results on Wednesday.
CoinShares reported treasury holdings of 6,562 Ether (ETH) at a fair value of $17.6 million and 50,213 Solana (SOL) valued at $5.9 million as of Sept. 30. The company also held 235 Bitcoin (BTC) worth $19.6 million at quarter-end.
CoinShares’ board approved up to $40 million in buybacks on Oct. 22 under a five-year authorization that shareholders granted in September. The authorization covers up to 32.9 million shares, or 25% of shares outstanding. The $40 million program runs until the company’s next annual meeting, expected in the second quarter of 2027.
“That’s nearly half of the $40 million authorized by the Board and gives us the flexibility to act when conditions allow,” said Jean-Marie Mognetti, co-founder, president and CEO of CoinShares, referring to the sale proceeds in a Wednesday press release.
CoinShares also reported $7.4 billion in total assets under management, up from $5.5 billion at the end of June, driven by rising crypto prices and $125 million in net inflows during the quarter. Revenue fell 45% from a year earlier to $27.7 million, including $19.1 million in asset management fees.
CoinShares’ shares fell 5.41% to close at $3.15 on Tuesday, ahead of the earnings report, leaving them down 63% from their $8.61 close on the company’s April 1 Nasdaq debut.
Related: Crypto adoption blooming in Germany, while UK is falling ‘behind,’ says CoinShares researcher

articles.title: Movie2K Defendant Could Hand Over 40,000 Bitcoin to End Trial—and Stay a Billionaire - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- A Leipzig judge has offered to end the trial of the alleged Movie2K operator if he hands over 40,000 BTC and pays €38 million ($42 million).
- Prosecutors believe the 43-year-old still holds around 56,000 BTC, meaning he could keep around 16,000 BTC, worth roughly €940 million ($1 billion).
- The deal comes as Germany prepares new powers to seize crypto of unclear origin, after selling nearly 50,000 BTC from the same case in 2024.
The alleged operator of defunct movie piracy site Movie2K could walk away from his trial in Germany and remain a billionaire, under a deal offered by the judge in the case.
The presiding judge at the Leipzig Regional Court has offered to drop tax evasion and money laundering charges against the 43-year-old main defendant if he hands over 40,000 BTC, public broadcaster MDR reported last week. He would also have to pay €38 million ($42 million) in compensation for potential victims, according to MDR.
Saxony's Office of the Public Prosecutor General confirmed the offer to news agency dpa, tech outlet heise reported on Tuesday. The 40,000 BTC would be worth around €2.36 billion ($2.6 billion) at current prices, according to heise.
But prosecutors believe the defendant holds a total of about 56,000 BTC. If he accepts, he could keep around 16,000 BTC, worth roughly €940 million ($1 billion) today and more than €1 billion when the offer was made.
A co-defendant has been offered a deal to hand over 600 BTC and pay €17 million ($19 million), and his lawyer said she could accept it, according to MDR. The main defendant's lawyers are considering the offer. The trial resumes on December 3 and could end before Christmas.
BTC price on November 22, 4:59PM UTC
Charges hard to prove
Movie2K offered hundreds of thousands of pirated films before shutting down in 2013. Its operators made money from advertising and subscription traps, and invested much of it in Bitcoin when it traded far below today's prices.
The copyright violations are time-barred, so the trial, which began in February, has focused on money laundering and tax evasion. The judge has reportedly expressed doubts about proving some of the charges, in part because legally and illegally acquired Bitcoin may have been mixed in the defendant's accounts, heise reported.
The main defendant was arrested abroad in 2023, and in early 2024 handed over nearly 50,000 BTC. Authorities in Saxony sold the coins later that year, raising about €2.64 billion ($2.9 billion), which is held in a state judicial treasury account. The money still belongs to the defendant until there is a final ruling, according to heise. Germany's government was left holding less than $300 million in Bitcoin after the sales.
Blockchain analytics firm Arkham said last year that German authorities had failed to seize some 45,000 BTC linked to the site.
The offer comes days after German lawmakers approved new powers allowing customs officials to seize assets, including crypto, of doubtful origin without first opening a criminal case. Under that law, owners of significant assets would have to show they were lawfully obtained.

articles.title: Russia Crypto Registry Raises Sanctions Fears Ahead of Launch
articles.text:
Sanctions fears loom over Russia’s regulated crypto trading launch
Russia’s crypto trading rollout faces uncertainty as companies weigh sanctions exposure, while Moscow Exchange prepares to launch crypto trading in December.
Russia’s push to bring cryptocurrency trading under government oversight is raising concerns that greater transparency could expose market participants to international sanctions.
Some companies are reluctant to join the Bank of Russia’s public registry of crypto exchangers because they fear becoming sanctions targets, a person familiar the regulatory discussions told Cointelegraph on Wednesday.
Industry representatives repeatedly asked the central bank to keep the registry private, but the regulator refused, arguing that crypto businesses should follow the same requirements as traditional financial service providers, the source said.
The concerns come as the European Union prepares its 22nd sanctions package against Russia, which is expected to include new restrictions on crypto platforms.
Russia’s crypto registry grows to 30 but trading launch remains blurry
Russia’s new rules allowing retail investors to buy Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and Tether’s USDt (USDT) took effect on Monday, and the central bank’s registry listed 30 authorized exchange operators as of Wednesday.
The list includes major lenders Sberbank and VTB, but registration alone does not establish whether customers can already complete transactions.
Related: KuCoin suspends services in Russia and Belarus
Alexander Nam of HSE University’s Center for Decentralized Finance and Digital Financial Assets Research said the market still faces technical and regulatory hurdles, including investor testing, order execution, settlement and custody.
“Being included in the registry does not in itself mean readiness to fully serve investors,” Nam told Cointelegraph.
Alexander Brazhnikov of the Russian Association of Cryptocurrency and Blockchain told Cointelegraph that he could not identify a registered operator offering confirmed retail access as of Monday.
EU sanctions plans loom over Russia’s December crypto launch
Moscow Exchange (MOEX), Russia’s main securities trading venue, plans to launch crypto trading on Dec. 1, with investors accessing the market through brokers rather than directly through the exchange. Cointelegraph contacted VTB, T-Invest Lab and MOEX for further details on their respective crypto trading launch plans but had not received responses by publication time.
The European Commission reportedly plans to present its next sanctions package ahead of a Nov. 26–27 European Council summit, days before MOEX’s scheduled launch.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday that Western sanctions had backfired and strengthened Russia’s economy, speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
Russia’s broader crypto activity has declined despite its push to establish a regulated trading market. The value of cryptocurrency transactions fell 14.7% to $284.1 billion in the year ended June 2026, according to Chainalysis. The country still accounted for roughly 44% of Eastern Europe’s crypto activity.

articles.title: Morning Minute: Nvidia Beats, Board Says ‘No’ on Jensen - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors fall despite NVDA beat, SOL leads; BTC at $64k
- NVDA delivers best earnings ever, targets 75% yoy growth; NVDA +3%
- OpenAI releases newest models GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, 1 day before ANT IPO
- Stanley Druckenmiller warns 2nd half of 2027 “could be economically disappointing”
- BTC ETF outflows continue with another $249M exodus
🖥️ Nvidia Beats, Board Says ‘No’ on Jensen
Six days after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago, Nvidia delivered the best quarter in its history. And told him he isn’t coming back.
The numbers first.
- Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, against roughly $109.1 billion expected.
- Data center alone was $107.6 billion, up 110% and now 93% of the company.
- GAAP net income of $65.3 billion, more than double last year.
- Adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share against $2.47 expected.
Fourth-quarter guidance came in at $130 billion against the $125.3 billion Wall Street wanted, with China assumed at zero.
And the CFO raised their 2028 revenue outlook to 75% year-over-year growth.
Just an absolute smash all around.
Then board chair Harvey Jones got on the call and said it plainly. “The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” The directors unanimously accepted his resignation, and Jones declined to answer anything about the circumstances or the independent investigation still running.
Huang had publicly offered to come back hours earlier, saying he would do it if directors believed it served shareholders and employees. Trump and Elon Musk both backed the idea. A petition passed 182,000 signatures including nearly 9,000 self-identified Nvidia employees. None of it moved the room.
Nvidia has hired Heidrick & Struggles to run the permanent search. Colette Kress stays interim CEO while remaining CFO, with Jones saying the board has “every confidence in Colette’s leadership, integrity and ability to deliver.” The board also created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, to receive reports from the company’s national security and trade compliance teams.
And after all of that—the stock rose about 3%.
A 6% revenue beat, guidance $5 billion above consensus, a new product cycle shipping, and the market gave it two percent. Shares sit roughly 35% below their October peak near $240. Nvidia perps on Hyperliquid were doing nearly a billion dollars of daily volume through the week, bouncing off $150 before settling near $162.
As for impact on the broader AI trade, Nvidia proved AI demand is not collapsing. You cannot manufacture $107.6 billion of data center revenue, and margins at 74.8% mean nobody is discounting to move product. The demand-collapse thesis died on Tuesday.
Two details do belong to the bears though. Growth is decelerating from 103% to roughly 77% once you strip the extra week out of Q4 guidance. And gross margin guides down about three points, from 74.8% to between 71% and 72%. Slowing growth plus compressing margins is how multiples come down regardless of how big the absolute numbers get.
The honest read is that the AI business is fine and the AI trade has stopped responding to it. For crypto that matters more than it should, because the correlation that dragged Bitcoin from $87,000 to the low $60s over six weeks ran through this exact trade.
Now we wait for the Fed on December 9 and insight into the 2027 rate hike cycle (or lack thereof) to determine the likely near-term fate.
🌎 Macro, Crypto and Markets
- Crypto majors are slightly red; BTC -1% at $64k; ETH -2% at $1,795; SOL +1% at $74; HYPE -1% at $68.6; ZEC -2% at $936
- FLR (+3%), Render (+4%), and XRP (+1.3%) led top alt movers
- Oil -1% at $85; Gold -2.4% at $3,770
- Stock futures are green after NVDA’s earnings beat; DOW even, Nasdaq +0.9%
- OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting Astra’s input pricing 20% to $8 per million tokens while scoring 62 on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index against Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 at 65; Astra is OpenAI’s first externally released model rated High for AI self-improvement, and showed no gain in coding-agent performance
- Amazon and Alphabet will own a combined 28.4% of Anthropic after its IPO, per the company’s S-1; both stakes are non-voting Class N shares, and a single Class F share held by the founders carries 50.1% of voting power
- Stanley Druckenmiller said he’s short copper and warned the second half of 2027 “could be economically disappointing,” pointing to a Fed that’s done cutting, weakening commodities, and widening credit spreads
- The World Bank Group said it will explore using Circle’s USDC and blockchain rails to disburse development funds, with Circle minting and settling and Citi supplying connections to traditional banking rails
- Glassnode said Bitcoin’s realized losses relative to realized profits have reached levels seen only near the lows of 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023
- ARK Invest sold 543,092 Nvidia shares worth about $84.8 million the day before earnings and put roughly $39.9 million into Block, Circle and Coinbase
- Ethereum developers flagged that two proposed changes in the Glamsterdam upgrade could break smart contracts, with EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 raising the gas limit while altering protocol assumptions that an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 contracts depend on
- MEXC is shutting down its Global Card today at 15:30 UTC after its third-party issuer pulled service, with existing cards going dead for transactions and new applications suspended
- Singapore’s top bank DBS is letting institutional clients mint and redeem USDC directly through a new Circle partnership; the 24/7 dollar-to-USDC settlement cuts institutional reliance on secondary-market liquidity for treasury and payment flows
Corporate Treasuries & ETFs
- The Bitcoin ETFs saw $249M in net outflows on Tuesday; the ETH ETFs saw $29M in outflows
Meme Coin Tracker

- Robinhood chain leaders were mostly red; Pons -1% to $78M; Cashcat -7% at $44M; AI -5% at $25M; Orbio -1% at $18M; HOOKR +25% and UBIK +10% were top movers
- Solana top movers included GTAVI +60x, GTA +44x, Leonida +43x and Dacity +26%; Stonk +2% at $34M, Ansem -3% at $44M

- Mantle’s MNT token officially entered the Japanese market, listed on the GMO Coin exchange

articles.title: How To Preserve Wealth And Access It During A National Emergency
articles.text:
How to preserve wealth and access funds during a national emergency
As geopolitical and technological threats multiply, the big question is whether you can hold on to your wealth and access funds when the system fails.
Amid kinetic war, cyberattacks and the prospect of the power grid failing, governments around the world have been encouraging citizens to prepare for major disruption.
In the UK, citizens have been stocking up on tinned food and bottled water in response to the government’s Be Ready campaign.
With fighter jets streaking across the skies of the Middle East, talk of a dirty bomb attack on Washington and the world’s largest software company going offline for a day, the possibility of disaster striking close to home is starting to look more realistic.
But what do you do with your money in times like these? How can you protect your wealth, but still be able to access it when the system fails?
There are two key aspects: choosing assets that maintain value even as the world goes up in flames, and being able to access funds during an emergency.
On the first point Maximilian Kunkel, chief investment officer for ultra-high-net-worth clients at UBS Global Wealth Management, tells Magazine, “We would caution against thinking of any single asset as ‘safe’ in all circumstances.”
Instead, he says wealthy investors should focus on building a portfolio that is “resilient across different scenarios,” with enough liquidity and diversification across asset classes, currencies and geographies.
Bitcoin, gold and the limits of ‘safe’ havens
The corporation’s 2026 global family office report, representing families with an average net worth of $2.7 billion, found 64% cited major geopolitical conflict as a concern over the next 12 months. These investors are not flocking to crypto for wealth preservation however.
“24% of family offices reported exposure to crypto or digital assets, but among those invested, allocations were typically only around 1%.”
Hadley Stern, head of institutions at Silence Laboratories and founder of Fidelity Digital Assets, explains that financial institutions may now place Bitcoin in the same category as gold, but it does not yet enjoy the same reputation as a safe haven.
“Gold has thousands of years of history [...] Bitcoin has less than two decades. But the reasoning people use is the same: a scarce asset that isn’t anyone else’s liability,” he says.
Related: Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?
He advises against using it as a reliable hedge in a crisis; “I’d be careful with the hedge story,” he says. “Bitcoin is still volatile, and in a sell-off it often trades like other risk assets.”
Cash, by contrast, is handy for emergencies “for liquidity and paying bills,” but not for “holding value over long stretches,” he says.
Michael D’Alessio, chief operating officer at digital asset trading platform Talos, tells Magazine, there are early signs that Bitcoin is beginning to behave more like gold. He said that through the volatility around the US midterm elections Bitcoin’s correlation with equities remained high. However, over the same period, its correlation with gold also rose sharply, to around 0.75 on a 30-day basis as of early August:
“That’s a meaningful shift, and it’s exactly the kind of signal institutional desks are now watching.”
BTC vs gold, 30-day rolling correlation of daily returns. Source: Talos/Coin Metrics
The risk is not just losing money; it’s losing access
The collapse of Mt Gox, or more recently the failure of Paraguay’s Ueno Bank show that “the asset is only as safe as the system holding it,” according to Stern.
Rather than automatically moving into Bitcoin or gold when tensions rise, risk committees are asking different questions:
“Where is the asset? Which jurisdiction is it in? Who can freeze it? What happens if a counterparty or a payment rail is down for a week?” he says. “Those used to be back-office questions. Now they come up at the board level.”
Kunkel said that concern over major geopolitical conflict is encouraging wealthy families to consider “not only asset allocation, but also where assets are held, currency exposure, liquidity and jurisdictional diversification.”
The UBS report found that 88% of family offices hold bankable assets in two or more jurisdictions, while 30% are increasing or considering increasing currency diversification.
Related: Half of UK wealth advisers say clients’ crypto is ‘invisible’ to them: CoinShares survey
The institutional version of a full pantry
Fortunately the banks and custody providers are making practical disaster preparations too.
“Regulators expect firms to plan for severe but plausible events,” Stern explains, such as a cloud outage, a cyberattack, a key vendor failing or a market closed for days, and “show they can keep their most important services running through them.”
The UK government is advising citizens to stock up on supplies. Source: Gov.uk
For custody providers, that means testing whether assets can still be moved if a signing location goes offline, and how quickly operations can recover if a data center is lost. Stern says while households might prep for an emergency by stocking a full pantry:
“The institutional version is not depending on any single thing: one custodian, one key holder, one cloud, one bank.”
Similarly investors need to work out which assets you can reach quickly and which you can’t, and “keeping enough liquidity to get through a bad stretch without being forced to sell.”
Kunkel says capital preservation “does not mean eliminating volatility, but maintaining enough liquidity and diversification to withstand volatility” without becoming a forced seller.
When the balloon goes up, diversification can protect a portfolio from a market shock, but it can’t guarantee access to funds if the infrastructure supporting it fails. A safe haven isn’t just about owning the right things; it’s about being able to access them when the system stops working.
Magazine: Banks are banning AI agents over security... and competition concerns

articles.title: 'Doomed From the Start': President Trump's Meme Coin Hits New Lows After Midterms - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- President Trump’s TRUMP meme coin hit an all-time low of $0.896 over the weekend and is down almost 40% since the midterms.
- Analysts say the Democrats taking Congress, and their plans to use subpoena power on Trump’s crypto ventures, add more pressure.
- They expect the token to keep declining whether or not Trump is in office, pointing to its lack of utility and a large share of supply still to unlock.
President Trump's official meme coin has reached new lows since he suffered a major blow in the U.S. midterm elections. The token has dropped almost 40% since election day, and analysts warn that new congressional scrutiny could push it lower.
Over the weekend, the TRUMP coin touched $0.896, marking the lowest point the token had ever stooped. It has since bumped 8%, sitting at $0.965, which is still down almost 40% from election day and 98.7% from its all-time high of $73.43, set the day after it launched, per Decrypt data.
Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt the midterms "added pressure to an already struggling token." Trading volume increased around the vote, and he believes some traders had bet on a Republican surprise win. He said there was a "visible unwind" that led to a "sharp drawdown" after the election results rolled out.
"Democrats take both chambers in January and plan to use their subpoena power on his crypto ventures. His net approval rating has almost never been lower," Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt. "It is still possible this continues to decline and, therefore, has a negative effect on these Trump-affiliated assets."
Other Trump-linked assets have also taken a hit. Since the election, World Liberty Financial's WLFI token has dropped 7.5%, per Decrypt data, and shares of the Trump Media & Technology Group have dropped 32%.
What is TRUMP?
Trump launched TRUMP on January 17, 2025, three days before his second inauguration, which Shannon described as "close to the peak of his popularity." Since then, the coin has faced significant scrutiny over how much the President and his family have profited from it. (The First Lady following suit and launching her own meme coin didn't help matters.)
The president’s crypto ventures also became a sticking point for the Clarity Act, a bill that aimed to provide a formal legal structure for most cryptocurrency activity. Democrats scrutinized the Trump family's involvement in the crypto industry, which profited them more than $1 billion in a year.
A July draft would have barred public officials and employees, along with their spouses, from issuing or sponsoring digital assets while in office. That draft didn’t extend to officials’ children, including Don Jr. and Eric Trump, and the provision would have expired in January 2029.
The bill failed a key Senate procedural vote in September. Patrick Witt, former executive director of the President’s Council of Advisers for Digital Assets, later said the “political issue of ethics really consumed everything else.”
TRUMP has "no value accrual, and it has been left in the dust of this narrative," Shannon said. "Google Trends shows searches for $TRUMP essentially flatlining since June 2025."
Nolan agreed, saying the coin’s appeal was "largely speculative," with no clear link between holding it and sharing in any underlying business success. The most it offered, he said, was the exclusive dinner to the top holders, which was both popular and controversial, depending on who you asked.
"In my view, that was just an attempt to prop up the token without actually creating any long-term demand for it," he said.
Interest in these dinners has dried up too. Ahead of the third gala scheduled for the event of the month, 185 holders of the token were invited to register, but only 130 wallets showed on the final leaderboard. Those wallets held a combined $8.6 billion worth of TRUMP, according to Reuters, which is a 94% decline from the first dinner.
Then there's the "unappealing" token supply structure, Nolan said. The majority of tokens were allocated to Trump-linked entities and are being slowly unlocked, which means demand needs to keep growing to soak up newly injected supply.
"That is a difficult position for an asset whose main attraction is attention around one individual," he said.
And what happens when Trump loses power? He has said he "would love" to serve a third term, but that remains unconstitutional—so the clock is ticking on his presidency.
"I think overall Trump leaving office probably means the token continues its gradual decline," Nolan told Decrypt. "Any big Trump headlines probably make it experience the same dead cat bounces (sharp rallies) we have seen it have during short periods of time."
Shannon thinks Trump doesn't even need to lose power for the token to keep going down. He said that it is "incredibly unlikely" that the token reclaims its highs, as it would require it to boost 82x, too many investors have been burned, and the majority of the supply is still to be unlocked.
"I think the meme coin was doomed from the start, and like with most meme coins, creating long-term demand is a Sisyphean task," Nolan told Decrypt.

articles.title: AI Will Make the Next 12 Months 'a Slaughterhouse' for Crypto Security: Anchorage Exec - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Anchorage Digital's Diogo Mónica warned that AI tools that can find and exploit vulnerabilities on their own will make the coming year "absolutely brutal."
- Solana Foundation security chief Michael Coates said more than $7.5 billion in crypto has been stolen this year, most of it in the Binance hack.
- Coates pointed crypto teams to the foundation's free STRIDE security framework, while both executives urged firms to lock down devices and keys.
Crypto companies face a wave of AI-powered attacks over the coming year, on top of an already relentless threat from North Korea, security leaders warned at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.
"The next 12 months are going to be absolutely brutal," said Diogo Mónica, co-founder of crypto bank Anchorage Digital. "They're going to be a slaughterhouse."
Over the past three to six months, AI systems have gone from finding vulnerabilities to building full exploits and carrying out every step of an attack on their own, Mónica said on a panel chaired by Gordon Corera, co-host of The Rest Is Classified podcast. Aggressive hacking tools now let anyone with no security knowledge simply tell a model to "please hack this website," he said.
Michael Coates, chief information security officer at the Solana Foundation, said AI has "dramatically lowered the cost and the barrier to hacking." Projects that once escaped attention will now be targeted opportunistically, he said.
'Part of their GDP'
North Korea remains the biggest threat to crypto firms, Coates said in a separate presentation. More than $13 billion in crypto has been stolen over the past decade, over $7.5 billion of it this year alone, with some $6 billion drained in a single breach: last month's hack of Binance, which the FBI has blamed on North Korea. "This is how they fund their programs in North Korea," he said.
Coates described the Binance attack as a chain of familiar tactics. A developer downloaded poisoned software from a sponsored search result, and an engineer later took a job interview on a work device and downloaded software as part of it. That gave the attackers a foothold to move through the network and reach signing services, which they used to authorize malicious transactions rather than steal the keys themselves, he said.
Fake job interviews are a "telltale tactic of North Korea," he said, along with poisoned tools and deepfake video calls. North Korean hackers have stolen $400 million using deepfake calls alone. When North Korean operatives can't get hired directly, they use people in the U.S. to take jobs on their behalf, then connect remote keyboards and mice so attackers can access the company's network, Mónica said.
The U.S. Treasury recently sanctioned 11 people over just such a North Korean IT worker scheme. Anchorage now onboards new staff in person at its U.S. office, Mónica added, and every employee works on a locked-down Chromebook, logging into remote machines for development, which he said removes 90% to 95% of its corporate attack surface.
'Protect the keys'
Coates pointed teams to STRIDE, a free security framework the Solana Foundation launched in the spring. It sets out 18 core controls tailored for crypto, and protocols covering more than 74% of DeFi's total value locked on Solana, including 10 of the top 11, have gone through it, he said. The foundation is also using AI to reverse-engineer newly launched programs and find flaws before attackers do, which he said has prevented more than $5 million in potential losses in the past month.
Both executives warned against basic mistakes. Connecting email inboxes to AI agents invites prompt injection attacks, Mónica said, while Coates urged teams to "protect the keys," using hardware security keys for logins and properly configured multisig wallets, with plans for key rotation and loss. "That's where we see the attackers going," Coates said. "They're getting the entry points through the basics. They're pivoting around to get the keys, and that's where they're unleashing their fury."

articles.title: Nvidia’s Tokenized Stock Market Cap Jumps 159% to $402M
articles.text:
Tokenized Nvidia market cap surges 159% amid Jensen Huang’s exit
Nvidia stock tokens reached $401.9 million in combined value as Jensen Huang stepped down and the chipmaker posted record quarterly revenue.
The combined market value of tokenized stocks tied to Nvidia shares rose about 159% from Nov. 8 to Tuesday, while the chipmaker’s Nasdaq-listed shares fell nearly 17% from their last close before co-founder Jensen Huang publicly admitted to an extramarital affair.
The value of Nvidia (NVDA) tokens tracked by Token Terminal rose from $155 million on Nov. 8 to $401.9 million by Tuesday.
Nvidia shed about $750 billion in market value, falling from $4.5 trillion at the Nov. 6 close to $3.75 trillion at Tuesday’s close, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to Nvidia employees on Nov. 8, nearly two weeks after The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang of spying for Beijing. China denied the allegations.
Related: ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results
Nvidia supplies chips that cloud providers such as Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure use to train and run AI models, making its earnings a gauge of global spending on AI infrastructure.
Tokenized stocks are blockchain tokens designed to track the price of a share. In one common setup, an issuer creates tokens backed by shares held by a custodian.
Binance, for example, lists an Nvidia token that can trade when Nasdaq is closed. It gives investors exposure to Nvidia’s share price without shareholder rights. The market value can rise as more tokens enter circulation, even if Nvidia’s share price falls.
Nvidia posts record revenue after Huang’s exit
Huang resigned as president and CEO of Nvidia and stepped down from the company’s board Thursday. Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.
On Tuesday, Nvidia’s board said it “does not intend to reinstate” Huang, shortly after the chipmaker reported record third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and above Wall Street estimates. Data center sales more than doubled to $107.6 billion, accounting for about 93% of total revenue. Nvidia forecast fourth-quarter sales of about $130 billion.
Nvidia’s shares rose 2.82% to $159.80 in Wednesday premarket trading as of 12:50 pm UTC (07:50 am ET), according to Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Bitwise Seeks Texas Stock Exchange Listing for Zcash ETF
articles.text:
Bitwise seeks Texas Stock Exchange listing for Zcash ETF
Coinbase Custody would safeguard the fund’s ZEC holdings, while Bitwise Investment Advisers would serve as its manager and sponsor.
Bitwise Asset Management is seeking to list a spot Zcash exchange-traded fund (ETF) on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE), according to a registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
The S-1 filing names TXSE as the anticipated listing venue for the Bitwise Zcash ETF, which would trade under the ticker ZEC. The fund would hold Zcash directly and seek to reflect the value of its holdings, minus operating expenses and liabilities.
Coinbase Custody would safeguard the fund’s ZEC tokens, while Bitwise Investment Advisers would serve as its manager and sponsor.
The Bitwise fund has not begun trading, and its registration statement has yet to become effective. Its proposed annual sponsor fee also remains unspecified. The public filing also follows an Oct. 16 draft that identified NYSE Arca as the proposed exchange.
The filing comes as asset managers continue to expand their Zcash-linked investment products in the US.
Grayscale launched its Zcash ETF on NYSE Arca in August, becoming one of the first issuers to offer investors exposure to the cryptocurrency through a US-listed ETF. Meanwhile, Winklevoss Asset Services filed in October to launch a competing spot Zcash ETF on Nasdaq under the ticker WINK.
Related: Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade

articles.title: Scattered Spider Hacker Sentenced to 6 Years Over $11.6M in Stolen Crypto - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Tyler Buchanan, a 24-year-old Scot, was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison for a scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto.
- Buchanan and his co-conspirators phished employees at a dozen companies, then used stolen data and SIM swaps to break into victims' crypto wallets.
- He is the last of five defendants to be sentenced in the case, which the Justice Department has linked to the Scattered Spider hacking group.
A Scottish hacker who was part of the Scattered Spider hacking collective has been sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison for his role in a scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto.
Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, was sentenced to 72 months by a federal judge in Santa Ana, California, on Tuesday, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California said. The judge set a restitution hearing for December 11. Buchanan began hacking as a teenager and was part of Scattered Spider, the group of young, English-speaking hackers blamed for a string of high-profile cyberattacks, the BBC reported.
British national sentenced to six years in federal prison for hacking into companies and stealing at least $11 million in virtual currency https://t.co/h7oprrXcVK
— US Attorney L.A. (@USAO_LosAngeles) November 18, 2026
Buchanan pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. At the time, prosecutors said the scheme had stolen at least $8 million in crypto. That figure has since risen to at least $11.6 million.
Phishing texts and SIM swaps
Between September 2021 and April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing text messages to employees of at least a dozen companies, including telecoms, technology firms and crypto companies, according to the indictment and Buchanan's plea agreement. The messages linked to fake websites that captured employees' login details, which were sent to a Telegram channel run by Buchanan and another co-conspirator.
The group used information stolen from those companies to identify individual crypto holders, then carried out SIM swaps, tricking mobile carriers into moving victims' phone numbers to devices they controlled so they could intercept two-factor authentication codes and empty victims' wallets.
In the largest single theft, one victim lost $1.67 million in December 2022, according to the BBC. When authorities searched Buchanan's home in Scotland in April 2023, they found the names and addresses of numerous victims, and a text file containing crypto seed phrases and login details for one victim's account, prosecutors said.
"Those thefts had severe, life-altering consequences for many victims," prosecutors argued in a sentencing memo.
Five defendants sentenced
Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, which the Justice Department charged in November 2024. A Justice Department spokesperson confirmed at the time that the defendants were suspected members of Scattered Spider, the group behind high-profile attacks including the 2023 breach of MGM Resorts. Buchanan was arrested at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain in May 2024 while trying to board a private flight to Naples, the BBC reported, and has been in U.S. custody since April 2025.
His co-defendant Noah Urban, of Palm Coast, Florida, is serving 10 years in prison, while Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy and Evans Onyeaka Osiebo were each sentenced to 45 months, and Joel Martin Evans to two years.
U.S. authorities have continued to pursue alleged Scattered Spider members. In July, a 19-year-old suspect was extradited from Finland over an $8 million crypto ransom demand against a luxury jeweler.

articles.title: Bitcoin launches Testnet5 and gives miners a real trial of four proposed fixes
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Testnet5 enforces four proposed Bitcoin rules from block one, giving mining pools a way to test their block-building software.
- The minimum difficulty rises from 1 on Testnet4 to roughly 1 million on Testnet5 to curb rapid early mining.
- Bitcoin Core and Sparrow Wallet still have open Testnet5 proposals, with early node sync and wallet tests already reported.
Bitcoin miners have a new network, Testnet5, where they can test their software against four proposed changes to Bitcoin’s rules, with support in Bitcoin Core and Sparrow Wallet at the patch stage.
The Bitcoin Improvement Proposals repository added the record of Testnet5’s first block to the network specification on Nov. 17, three days after the block was mined.
What Bitcoin miners can test
The four changes are collectively known as BIP54, or Consensus Cleanup. Bitcoin Inquisition’s signet already enforces them, but producing blocks there also requires miners to satisfy a signing challenge in addition to proof of work.
On Testnet5, independent miners and pools can use their own software to build blocks and see whether other nodes accept them without that extra requirement.
Two of the four rules limit how much work certain blocks can impose on nodes and how miners can use timestamps to influence difficulty. One caps certain signature operations in ordinary transactions to limit how long a block can take to verify.
The other restricts timestamps at the start and end of each difficulty period to prevent miners from artificially driving the difficulty down.
A third rule rejects transactions that measure exactly 64 bytes after removing witness data, closing an ambiguity in proofs of transaction inclusion. The fourth makes each new mining reward transaction unique by requiring its locktime to equal the block height minus one and requiring that locktime to take effect.
Pool operators can use Testnet5 to check that their software, which usually builds the reward transaction, applies the new rule.
Testnet4 let miners drop to minimum difficulty if a block’s timestamp was more than 20 minutes after the previous one, except at the start of a difficulty period. BIP95 says competing blocks mined under the exception caused frequent short reorganizations, where one set of recent blocks replaced another.
Testnet5 removes the 20-minute rule altogether and raises the minimum difficulty from 1 to about 1 million. The specification’s authors chose the higher floor to slow early block production before difficulty adjusts, while keeping it low enough for a single specialized mining machine to keep the test chain running.
Early testers can build the Bitcoin Core patch and sync by manually connecting to a peer, its author reported. The proposal targets Core’s 32.x branch and still needs to be merged and shipped in a public release.
Bitcoin Core 32.1, the latest release as of Nov. 18, predates the Testnet5 integration build.
Sparrow’s wallet integration proposal opened late on Nov. 17, and would let users select Testnet5 in the wallet and add two public Electrum servers to connect to the chain.
A Sparrow collaborator reported on Nov. 18 that the wallet’s Silent Payments feature worked in tests against both servers. The proposal, which depends on an update to Sparrow’s Drongo library, remained open.

articles.title: Nvidia Sparks Stock-Market Relief With Bitcoin in ‘Bid-Heavy’ Environment
articles.text:
Bitcoin steadies after Nvidia’s earnings beat as $60K bids stand out
Bitcoin halted downside as Nvidia confidence returned, with its stock gaining 3% premarket and South Korea’s tech-heavy KOSPI reclaiming 5,000 points.
Bitcoin (BTC) steadied on Wednesday as US stock futures rose after Nvidia reported stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue.
Key points:
- Bitcoin returned to its $64,000–$66,000 trading range after Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in third-quarter revenue and forecast $130 billion for the fourth quarter.
- Nvidia shares rose about 3% in premarket trading on Wednesday, while South Korea’s KOSPI closed 2% higher at 5,067.
- Glassnode identified $60,000 as the lower end of a range where a further Bitcoin price drop could trigger long liquidations.
Nvidia stock gains 3% premarket
Data from TradingView showed Bitcoin returning to the $64,000–$66,000 range it had traded in since Nov. 15.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Bitcoin briefly fell below the range on Tuesday ahead of Nvidia’s earnings release. Nvidia then reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, above expectations of $108 billion, and forecast $130 billion for fourth quarter. Its shares rose about 3% to $160.60 in Wednesday’s premarket trading.
Nvidia futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
“Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” interim CEO Colette Kress commented in a press release.
The momentum was reflected in broader equities performance, with Nasdaq 100 futures gaining 1%. South Korea’s tech-heavy KOSPI Composite closed 2% higher at 5,067 Wednesday, bouncing back above 5,000 after its lowest daily close since February.
KOSPI one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Meanwhile, Nvidia’s board rejected calls to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang. On the earnings call, board chairman Harvey Jones said the directors had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation.
“I’m good with Colette. She is clearly competent and strong. I feel that Nvidia is in a good spot and over time the right leadership will emerge,” Ross Gerber, cofounder, CEO and CIO at investment manager Gerber Kawasaki, wrote on X. Gerber compared Kress to Apple CEO Tim Cook and called it a “new chapter” for Nvidia.
Glassnode flags $60,000 level for Bitcoin
Optimism allowed Bitcoin to stay above 18-week lows of $62,000 seen Sunday. Analyzing Binance order-book composition, crypto research platform Glassnode emphasized the importance of the area around the $60,000 mark.
Related: Bitcoin ETFs lose $240M as CryptoQuant flags bearish market phase
“Within 5% of price, resting bids on Binance and Coinbase now outweigh asks about 2.3x. Since late August, bids have usually outweighed asks only slightly,” it wrote in the latest edition of The Week Onchain newsletter.
“The brightest band on the heatmap, near $60K, is the largest single bid level on Binance since August.”
Binance BTC spot order-book liquidity data. Source: Glassnode
Glassnode flagged $60,000 as the lower end of a range where falling prices could force traders out of long positions and accelerate the sell-off. It added that the majority of forced position closures had “already happened” on the initial move down.
Bitcoin futures liquidation heatmap. Source: Glassnode

articles.title: World Bank, Circle, Citi Partner to Explore Stablecoins for Payments
articles.text:
World Bank partners with Circle, Citi to explore stablecoins for payments
The initiative builds on the World Bank’s existing blockchain platform, which aims to create more fund traceability for investments in developing countries.
The World Bank Group said Tuesday it would explore using Circle’s USDC stablecoin to get money to borrowing countries faster and at a lower cost.
The group will work with Citi and Circle to see how payments in stablecoins tied to the US dollar could fit into the banking network it already uses to send money abroad, according to a press release.
Circle would provide the tools for USDC (USDC) issuance and transfers, while Citi would connect the project to existing banking networks. The group plans to start with borrowing countries that allow the use of digital assets.
The World Bank is a development bank owned by its member countries. It lends to governments in low- and middle-income countries and gives grants to some of the poorest, helping fund schools, health clinics and clean water systems.
The bank began rolling out blockchain tool FundsChain in 2025 to let project teams and auditors see where the money goes. The bank says the tool now covers more than 350 projects in 96 countries.
The World Bank in 2023 warned that widespread use of stablecoins could displace local money and make it harder for central banks to manage economies.
In June, CGAP, a research group based at the World Bank, examined using stablecoins to deliver humanitarian aid. The report found that stablecoins can make it easier for an aid agency to move money across borders. However, when recipients are paid directly in stablecoins, they may have to pay to convert them to local currency.
Related: Abu Dhabi royal backs 49% stake in Trump-linked crypto bank venture: WSJ

articles.title: Japan bond yields surge to 3.75%, hiding a quiet Bitcoin trap
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Japan’s Nov. 18 auction drew competitive tenders worth 3.64 times the amount accepted, down from 5.84 for the same bond in October.
- The dollar-yen midpoint moved just ¥0.01 between the Bank of Japan’s two Tokyo readings, while overnight yen funding held steady.
- Japan’s Nov. 25 bond sale will test long-term demand, while yen funding and futures data matter more directly for Bitcoin leverage.
Demand fell at Japan’s Nov. 18 auction of a 20-year government bond, with investors offering to buy 3.64 times the amount the Finance Ministry accepted in the competitive auction, putting pressure on traders who borrow yen to hold Bitcoin.
The average accepted yield rose, while the yen barely moved between the Bank of Japan’s two 5 p.m. Tokyo readings.
In the Nov. 18 results, the ministry recorded ¥1.914 trillion in competitive tenders for issue 198 and accepted ¥525.8 billion. At the October auction, it received ¥3.139 trillion and accepted ¥537.1 billion.
Demand fell by much more than the amount sold in the competitive auction, and the average accepted yield rose 3.3 basis points to 3.756% from 3.723%.
Competitive coverage fell from 5.84× on Oct. 20 to 3.64× on Nov. 18 for Japan’s 20-year issue 198.
At 5 p.m. in Tokyo, the midpoint of the Bank of Japan’s dollar-yen quote was 159.35 yen per dollar on Nov. 18, up one hundredth of a yen from 159.34 on Nov. 17.
Money-market broker Tokyo Tanshi reported a weighted average unsecured overnight call rate of 1.227%, unchanged from the previous day. The rate measures one-day borrowing in Japan’s call money market, for which the Bank of Japan publishes a daily series.
What would put pressure on Bitcoin positions
A trader borrowing yen short-term to hold Bitcoin faces higher costs to renew the loan if funding rates rise. If the trader sells Bitcoin for dollars and leaves the yen debt unhedged, a stronger yen makes repaying the loan in dollar terms more expensive.
Bank for International Settlements researchers documented that feedback during the August 2024 unwind in leveraged currency and equity trades.
Bitfinex reported that aggregate Bitcoin futures open interest fell to 645,750 BTC over Nov. 14 and 15, 8% below Nov. 11. The futures total shows how much exposure was outstanding but gives no breakdown by funding currency.
BIS research showed that although it identified $271 billion in yen-denominated bank loans to non-bank borrowers outside Japan in the first quarter of 2024, it could not determine how much was used for carry trades.
The Finance Ministry plans to offer about ¥300 billion at the Nov. 25 reopening of a 40-year bond, the next test of long-dated demand.
A stronger signal for Bitcoin would be rising short-term yen borrowing costs or a sustained strengthening of the yen, alongside shrinking futures exposure and evidence that traders cutting positions had yen liabilities.

articles.title: Solana Outperforms Bitcoin and Ether During Breakpoint
articles.text:
SOL comes out of Breakpoint 7% higher as Solana exits beta
Solana’s token reached $75.12 on Tuesday, outpacing Bitcoin and Ether after the network retired the beta label it had used since its 2020 launch.
Solana’s native token gained nearly 7% over the three days of the network’s Breakpoint conference in London, outperforming Bitcoin and Ether.
Solana (SOL) rose to $75.12 on Tuesday, up 6.95% from $70.24 at the end of Saturday, according to CoinGecko data. Bitcoin gained 1.2% and Ether rose 3.1% over the same period.
Breakpoint opened with a pre-conference event on Sunday, followed by the main program on Monday and Tuesday.
SOL’s price increase coincided with several announcements at Breakpoint, including a milestone in Solana’s network development and new institutional initiatives.
On Monday, the Solana Foundation announced that its Solana 1.0 designation has formally replaced the “mainnet beta” label used since the network’s 2020 launch. The change marks Solana’s move out of beta after six years, without affecting how users interact with the network.
Meanwhile, Project Harmonia named its first cohort of asset managers. The initiative, led by Allfunds Blockchain and the Solana Foundation, aims to distribute funds tokenized on Solana through Allfunds’ institutional network.
Other plans had been disclosed ahead of Breakpoint. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation said Thursday it intends to connect its tokenization service to Solana in the second half of 2027.
Separately, Forward Industries announced a partnership with Groma to bring GromaCoin, a tokenized real estate asset, to Solana. Groma expects it to launch on the network in the first quarter of 2027.
Related: Solana Foundation takes majority interest in crypto data firm CoinGecko

articles.title: Bitwise offloads 23.7M XRP while silently stacking 126M more
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitwise sold 23.7 million XRP to fund third-quarter cash redemptions as its holdings grew by 126.3 million XRP.
- Franklin received 41.3 million XRP in kind and bought 26.6 million for creations, with zero third-quarter redemptions.
- The Nov. 17 ETF outflow estimates measure net withdrawals and leave the amount of XRP sold that day unresolved.
Bitwise’s quarterly filings show its XRP ETF sold 23.7 million XRP to meet cash redemptions from July through September 2026, even as the fund increased its holdings by 126.3 million XRP.
The quarter’s redemption sales slightly exceeded the 22.9 million XRP the fund sold for the same purpose in the entire first half of the year.
Bitwise’s holdings climbed from 286.8 million XRP at the end of June to 413.1 million at the end of September. The Sept. 30 quarterly report, filed Nov. 6, records both the XRP the fund sold for redemptions and the larger amount it added for new shares.
Subtracting the six-month XRP schedule from the nine-month schedule isolates what happened in the third quarter. Bitwise bought 87.9 million tokens to back newly issued shares and received another 62.3 million XRP in kind.
Together, those flows added 150.2 million tokens before the fund’s cash redemption sales and roughly 241,383 XRP transferred to pay sponsor fees. Bitwise reported zero in-kind redemptions for the quarter.
Bitwise created 13.75 million shares and redeemed 2.42 million, leaving a net increase of 11.33 million shares, an increase in shares that masks the gross redemptions that took place along the way.
The sponsor arranges a sale of the underlying XRP for a cash redemption and pays out the proceeds, less a transaction fee. In-kind redemption delivers the token itself to the authorized firm or its designee.
The Franklin Templeton XRP ETF’s third-quarter filing shows the firm issued 6.25 million shares in the quarter, including 3.8 million in kind and 2.45 million for cash. The fund received 41.3 million tokens in kind and bought 26.6 million for creations, and recorded zero share redemptions.
A separate Canary XRP ETF filing puts that fund’s cash redemption sales at 9.55 million XRP for the nine months through Sept. 30. Canary reported zero tokens delivered for in-kind redemptions over those nine months.
What Nov. 17 XRP outflows leave unresolved
In its Nov. 18 update, Crypto ETF’s fund table estimated $6.1 million in net outflows for Nov. 17 based on three of five tracked funds.
Alpha Finance’s daily figures also put the rounded net outflow at $6.1 million, with data for all five funds it tracks. Alpha Finance estimated $5 million in outflows from Canary and $1.1 million from Grayscale, compared with $4.9 million and $1.2 million in the Crypto ETF snapshot.
Canary’s daily share history shows 490,000 fewer shares outstanding on Nov. 17 than on Nov. 16. Bitwise’s fund data showed 36.44 million shares on Nov. 16 and 406.8 million XRP in its Nov. 17 holdings table.
If issuers break out the same categories in their next filings, it will be possible to measure sales for fourth-quarter redemptions and distinguish them from in-kind transfers and fees.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $240M as CryptoQuant Flags Bearish Phase
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs lose $240M as CryptoQuant flags bearish market phase
Bitcoin ETF outflows returned after a one-day pause as CryptoQuant warned that Bitcoin had returned to a bearish market phase.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) resumed logging net outflows on Tuesday after a brief pause in the bleeding to start the week.
The funds recorded around $240 million in net outflows on Tuesday, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounting for $210 million, according to Farside Investors data.
IBIT had $76.5 million in net inflows on Monday, ending a $2.35 billion net outflow streak that spanned 11-straight sessions.
US spot Ether (ETH) ETFs also recorded net outflows of $29 million on Tuesday, adding to $8.3 million in withdrawals Monday. The ETH funds have seen net outflows in eight of the last nine trading sessions.
The renewed outflows in crypto ETFs came amid ongoing weakness in Bitcoin (BTC), which briefly dipped below $63,000 on Tuesday, according to CoinGecko.
Bitcoin has returned to a bearish phase amid weakening demand and mounting investor losses, CryptoQuant said in a Tuesday report shared with Cointelegraph. Its Bitcoin Analyst Consensus Index showed sentiment at its most bearish level since November 2025.
“Bitcoin needs demand growth in order to recover and rally sustainably,” CryptoQuant said, noting that total Bitcoin demand growth was contracting at its fastest pace since July 1.
Despite the bearish signals, CryptoQuant identified potential price support between $62,000 and $65,000 but cautioned that the indicators did not yet confirm a market bottom.

articles.title: Strategy's STRC stock crashes to $95 despite promise of 44 years of dividends
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Michael Saylor's STRC fell to its lowest level since August despite Strategy spending $2.7 billion on buybacks.
- Strategy spent $1.4 billion buying STRC near $100, yet shares have plunged toward $95, pushing the annualized yield to roughly 12.5%.
- With just $332 million in buyback capacity left, Strategy faces questions over further repurchases as Peter Schiff warns of potential Bitcoin sales.
Strategy's (formerly MicroStrategy) STRC preferred stock plunged to its lowest level since August on Wednesday despite the company's multibillion-dollar repurchase campaign.
The Michael Saylor-led company's preferred shares fell to $95.51 before recovering to $96.16, according to Strategy's data. The decline left STRC roughly 4% below its $100 stated amount, pushing its annualized yield to approximately 12.5%.
Regular-session, unadjusted daily closes through Nov. 17. Nov. 18 is an incomplete trading day: final $97.00 point is a timestamped 12:39 p.m. ET intraday quote. The $100 series is STRC stated amount, and displayed prices are verified against Stock Analysis.
The selloff comes despite Strategy spending about $2.67 billion repurchasing STRC shares since July to stabilize the security near $100.
An earlier analysis found that the company spent about $1.4 billion on repurchases between Sept. 28 and Nov. 15, with weekly average purchase prices ranging from $99.06 to $99.93.
That accounted for more than half of its total repurchase spending, even as the discount to STRC's stated amount had nearly disappeared.
Open $98.50, high $98.69, low $95.50, latest available quote $97.00 at 12:39 p.m. ET. Bars are dollars below STRC’s $100 stated amount, and negative numbers are discounts.
This sustained intervention has left just $332.2 million available under its $3 billion preferred-stock repurchase authorization, raising questions about how much more capital Strategy will commit if selling pressure persists.
Strategy CEO defends STRC's dividend coverage
Despite the renewed weakness, Strategy CEO Phong Le has defended STRC's financial structure and its ability to generate income for investors.
In a Nov. 17 statement, Le said:
“STRC is Digital Credit: high income, low volatility, and 44 years of dividend coverage. Built for income investors as TradFi and DeFi converge.”
His assessment contrasts with economist Peter Schiff, who warned that the security's continued decline could eventually force Strategy to sell Bitcoin.
Schiff said:
“Despite the buybacks, $STRC is collapsing. At $96 the current yield is 12.5% and rising.”
Schiff argued that Strategy would have to exhaust its cash reserves to support the stock before selling Bitcoin to finance additional repurchases. He suggested raising or suspending dividends as an alternative.
However, Le's 44-year coverage assertion reflects Strategy's broader Bitcoin-backed financial capacity.
The company's latest disclosures showed that its $4.75 billion dedicated dollar reserve and $151.2 million in unrestricted cash provide approximately 3.4 years of coverage for preferred dividends and debt-interest obligations.
Strategy also held 850,849 BTC as of Nov. 15, providing another source of liquidity through potential asset sales.
The company has already authorized Bitcoin sales to support its preferred-stock obligations and repurchase programs, although it has recently relied more heavily on common-stock issuance.

articles.title: Ledger Hardware Wallet Tampering Fears Spread to Dubai
articles.text:
Ledger hardware implant saga reaches Dubai’s Virgin Megastore
Two Ledger owners reported losing a combined $604,000 in crypto from hardware wallets they said were purchased at authorized retailer Virgin Megastore in Dubai.
Two Ledger owners have reported cryptocurrency thefts involving hardware wallets they say were purchased from an authorized retailer in Dubai, raising concerns that a hardware wallet tampering campaign had also spread to the UAE.
An X user posting as Rewinsky on Monday said they found their Ledger Flex had been tampered with after reporting the loss of about 1,300 Solana (SOL). Mark Karpelès’ Ledger Implant OSINT registry subsequently confirmed the device as containing a hardware implant.
A second owner, posting as New Babylon Order Worldwide, said Tuesday that 507,000 USDt (USDT) was stolen from their Ledger Stax on Saturday. They said the device was bought new at Virgin Megastore Dubai on Oct. 11, two days after Ledger publicly disclosed an investigation into crypto losses involving devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.
The reports suggest the Ledger device tampering has extended past retailers in just Asia and Europe. Ledger lists Virgin Megastores among its authorized retailers in the United Arab Emirates.
Virgin Megastore lists eight stores in Dubai, including branches at Dubai Mall, Mall of the Emirates and Dubai Hills Mall.
Cointelegraph reached out to Ledger and Virgin Megastore for comment.
