articles.title: Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
articles.text:
President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small US and Philippine flags. A band played “YMCA,” a staple at Trump rallies, as more girls in traditional bell-sleeved blouses and young men in wide-brimmed hats danced to the song.
Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
Facing opposition at home, Trump is eyeing the former US colony to build chip fabs and data centers.
Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
Facing opposition at home, Trump is eyeing the former US colony to build chip fabs and data centers.
Outside the airport, hundreds of protesters packed streets bearing signs — and at least one prop casket — saying “Trump out.” Others say “Reject Pax Silica,” the name for the US-led international initiative to secure chips and critical minerals used in the hardware fueling the AI boom.
Peace and prosperity for whom?
“Pax” comes from the Latin word for “peace, stability, and long-term prosperity,” the Pax Silica website proudly says. Yet the unspoken question — peace and prosperity for whom? — explains the whiplash between the Philippine government’s warm welcome of Trump and the public fury raging outside.
Trump says he wants to “win AI” — whatever that means. As such, the US needs data centers full of GPUs to do it. With Americans increasingly opposed to data centers and chip factories being built in their communities, the US is now recruiting less affluent nations to take up some of the slack. Lawmakers from both the US and the Philippines are promising a slice of the riches that advances in generative AI are supposed to create. And that’s supposed to be worth the land razed, homes destroyed, and natural resources lost in the name of technological progress. In the Philippines, that’s taking the shape of a proposed 1,620-hectare (4,000 acres) hub for chip factories, processing plants for critical minerals, and data centers.
At least two dozen countries have signed on to the Pax Silica initiative, and Trump was expected to pressure more to join while in the Philippines for events related to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. With Pax Silica, the US aims to insulate itself from China’s dominance in manufacturing semiconductors and processing critical minerals needed to make those chips. Trump held a bilateral meeting with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen to meet with China’s President Xi Jinping and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin.
Philippine and US officials are expected to sign a framework agreement by the end of the year for the jointly developed Pax Silica Economic Security Zone. The details are still murky and shrouded in NDAs. The Philippines’ Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) overseeing the plan expects an economic boom from minerals processing and chip manufacturing, with perhaps a data center or two on site. Meanwhile, human rights advocates who oppose the project warn that it will displace Indigenous residents, cutting them off from water resources on which they rely.
“How do we give up our burial grounds, our church, our livelihood?”
“We do not want to give up our community,” Petronila Capiz-Muñoz, chieftain of the Indigenous Aeta Hungey tribe, told Human Rights Watch. “How do we give up our burial grounds, our church, our livelihood? This is where we source our water, this is where we plant.” Capiz-Muñoz said BCDA officials have told residents that they’ll need to relocate by December to make way for development. Small farmers are also afraid the semiconductor hub will push them off their lands, according to Lian Buan, Southeast Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch.
There are layers of land-grabbing to unpack here.
The Aeta are among the first people to inhabit the Philippines, believed to have arrived around 30,000 years ago. And yet the Aeta Hungey tribe has been trying since 1994 to secure an official certificate recognizing its ancestral domain in one of the areas now facing industrial development. But since the tribe hasn’t been granted that certificate, the BCDA can still claim the AI hub will be built “outside titled ancestral domains.”
The agency says the project will be on public land located at the former Clark Air Base built in the early 1900s when the Philippines was a US territory. The Philippine constitution now only allows its own citizens to own private land. But the BCDA can offer leases lasting as long as 99 years to foreign developers. The agency expects to rake in close to $1 billion USD (about 60 billion in PHP Peso) from lease income over the first 25 years.
There are layers of land-grabbing to unpack here
The BCDA was in talks with around 30 different companies interested in setting up shop in Clark’s proposed AI hub, then-BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang told reporters in July. He couldn’t name names, he said, because of NDAs — creating the same kind of opacity that has turned Americans against data centers on their home turf.
He did mention, however, that an American energy company was conducting a feasibility study into building a liquefied natural gas (LNG) line and plant to meet the hub’s enormous electricity demand. Bingcang called LNG a clean fuel, but that’s provably false. LNG is primarily methane, a smog-forming pollutant that is an even more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.
Bingcang said in September that the Philippine government wanted to invite Nvidia, TSMC, and Apple. While one or two data center developers had expressed interest, according to Bingcang, most of the companies interested were “high tech” manufacturing firms. He has also described chip manufacturing as a “clean” industry, echoing corporate spin that’s been around since the start of Silicon Valley.
At the first chip fabs in California, workers — many of them Filipino immigrants — donned “bunny suits” to assemble sensitive chips in environmentally controlled “clean rooms.” Little did they know that the gear they wore offered little protection against the harsh chemicals used in manufacturing, which also leaked out of storage tanks to contaminate soil and groundwater. When studies came out in the ’90s documenting disproportionately high rates of miscarriages among workers, companies pledged to phase out some of the chemicals linked to reproductive health risks. Around the same time, chip manufacturing started to move out of the US to Asia, where similar health problems stemming from the same chemicals cropped up even decades later.
Chipmakers say their fabs have gotten much safer over the years, in part because more work is automated. Even so, the BCDA estimates that the AI hub will create up to 190,000 direct jobs. The BCDA, White House, and Philippine’s Malacañang Palace did not immediately respond to questions from The Verge.
“I don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well. They were great,” Trump told President Marcos during his visit. Marcos’ parents are estimated to have stolen up to $30 billion from government coffers over decades of rule before a people power movement ousted the current president’s father from the same office in the 1980s. But public memory, it seems, can be short.
And skyrocketing demand for more powerful chips used for generative AI has raised fears among environmental and labor groups that history might repeat itself. Companies move fast and break things, leaving a toxic mess in their wake. And when Americans decide they’ve had enough in their own back yards, the industry sets up shop somewhere else where they think their customers aren’t paying attention and politicians are happy to look the other direction.

articles.title: Google's AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s search engine has long offered an incognito mode for all those search queries you don’t want logged or associated with your account. Now, Google’s AI Mode in Search is getting a similar feature. In a blog post, the company announced a new feature that brings “temporary threads” to AI Mode, where the conversations you have won’t be resurfaced later in areas like your search history or recommendations.
Many leading AI chatbots already offer the option for temporary chats, Google Gemini included. However, there was not yet an option to have a temporary chat when you’re searching Google and are dropped into its conversational interface, known as AI Mode.
Google says that users won’t have to adjust their settings to take advantage of the new option. Instead, they’ll be able to click a temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode to engage in a temporary chat. This essentially works the same as a temporary chat would in the stand-alone Gemini chatbot.
The option could be convenient to use at those times when you start digging deeper into a particular topic via AI Mode and realize that you don’t want the discussion to become a part of your search history because of its personal nature.
Once the temporary thread is started, the session becomes detached from your account, Google says. This means that the responses the AI provides won’t be informed by past preferences, nor will they impact future personalization. That could also be useful for those times when you want to learn about something as more of a one-off, but don’t want Google to start to think of the topic as one of your main interests.
When you close out of the thread, you will return to searching as usual.
The company says the option to engage in temporary chats in AI Mode is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile across all supported languages.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 18/11: Thế giới đi lên, trong nước mai điều chỉnh
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Giá dầu quốc tế trong phiên giao dịch 17/11 được điều chỉnh tăng nhẹ.
Ở phiên giao dịch 17/11, giá dầu Brent tăng 0,76%, đóng cửa ở mức 93,14 USD/thùng. Trong khi đó, giá dầu WTI tăng 0,34%, kết phiên ở mức 86,01 USD/thùng.
Đầu phiên giao dịch hôm nay (18/11), giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh đi xuống.
Theo dữ liệu từ Oilprice, vào lúc 6h28' ngày 18/11 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent vẫn được niêm yết ở mức 93,14 USD/thùng. Còn giá dầu WTI được điều chỉnh xuống mức 85,83 USD/thùng, giảm 0,21% so với phiên liền trước.
Giá dầu thế giới đi lên khi giới đầu tư lo ngại về những vụ tấn công nhằm vào tàu thuyền tại eo biển Hormuz làm gián đoạn nguồn cung dầu.
Ngày 17/11, các máy bay không người lái (UAV) của Iran đã tấn công một hệ thống radar quân sự của Mỹ tại Bahrain. Trong khi toàn bộ thủy thủ đoàn của một con tàu tại eo biển Hormuz vẫn chưa xác định được tung tích sau khi con tàu này bị tấn công hai lần.
Cũng trong ngày 17/11, quân đội Mỹ đã tiến hành các cuộc không kích mới nhằm vào Iran, để đáp trả các cuộc tấn công của Iran nhằm vào nhân viên và tài sản của Mỹ.
Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump ngày 17/11 cho biết Mỹ đang nghiêm túc xem xét khả năng Iran có thể đang lên kế hoạch thực hiện một cuộc tấn công bằng thứ được gọi là “bom bẩn” tại Washington.
Tuy nhiên, đà tăng của giá dầu phần nào bị hạn chế bởi dự báo nguồn cung toàn cầu dư thừa, trong bối cảnh hoạt động xuất khẩu dầu từ Trung Đông đang phục hồi.
Mới đây, Cơ quan Năng lượng Quốc tế (IEA) dự báo thị trường dầu mỏ toàn cầu sẽ quay trở lại trạng thái dư cung trong quý IV năm nay, do xuất khẩu dầu từ Trung Đông phục hồi nhanh hơn tốc độ tăng trưởng nhu cầu toàn cầu.
Các nước xuất khẩu dầu ở Trung Đông đã tăng lượng hàng xuất khẩu, đưa dòng chảy dầu tiến gần mức trước khi xung đột giữa Mỹ và Iran bùng phát hồi cuối tháng 2.
Ngày 16/11, Tổ chức Các nước Xuất khẩu Dầu mỏ (OPEC) đã tổ chức một cuộc họp trực tuyến để thảo luận về việc xem xét lại năng lực sản xuất bền vững tối đa của các thành viên, điều này sẽ giúp xác định hạn ngạch sản lượng của OPEC+ cho năm 2027 và những năm tiếp theo.
Nhóm OPEC+ (bao gồm cả Nga) dự kiến sẽ họp vào ngày 29/11 để quyết định chính sách sản lượng năm 2027.
Trong khi đó, tại Mỹ, kết quả từ cuộc khảo sát của Reuters cho thấy lượng dầu thô tồn kho được dự báo giảm.
Số liệu của Bộ Năng lượng Mỹ cho hay, lượng dầu trong Kho dự trữ dầu mỏ chiến lược (SPR) của nước này giảm xuống còn 276,4 triệu thùng trong tuần trước, mức thấp nhất kể từ tháng 8 năm 1982. Các đợt xuất kho gần đây nằm trong thỏa thuận của Mỹ về việc giải phóng 172 triệu thùng dầu từ kho dự trữ chiến lược này.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Theo kế hoạch, liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính sẽ tiến hành điều chỉnh giá xăng dầu trong nước vào chiều mai (19/11).
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (18/11) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 12/11, giá xăng E5RON92 được điều chỉnh giảm 1.499 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 19.399 đồng/lít.
Tương tự, giá xăng E10RON95-III hạ 1.311 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 19.845 đồng/lít.
Cùng xu hướng, giá dầu diesel 0.05S được điều chỉnh giảm 1.874 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 26.822 đồng/lít.
Còn giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S hạ 2.263 đồng/kg, giá bán không cao hơn 19.742 đồng/kg.
Theo dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: Workers now treat jobs like portfolios as AI hiring erodes trust
articles.text:
Survey data from thousands of professionals shows why many treat a second paycheck as unemployment insurance.
Ask a growing number of professionals about a second job, and many call it unemployment insurance. In an Enhancv survey of 1,000 professionals holding multiple full-time roles, 79.5% agreed a second paycheck protects them against layoffs and economic instability.
Hiring data explains why. According to a survey of 1,066 U.S. job seekers, 50.5% received a rejection with no human feedback in the past year. Workers once traded loyalty for job security, but many professionals now manage employment like a financial portfolio. In other words, they rely on income from several jobs so that losing one job doesn’t wipe out their earnings.
Silent Rejections
Hiring decisions now happen out of view. Among the 538 respondents who got silent rejections, 63.8% believed an algorithm made the call. Younger applicants experience silence more often than older ones. Silent rejections reached 62.2% of applicants aged 25 to 34 and 61.5% of those aged 18 to 24, compared with 32% of those 55 and older.
Employers rarely disclosed AI use, according to 68.5% of candidates. Among respondents, 31.4% abandoned an application after a one-way video or chatbot screen, and nearly half of respondents (47.7%) agreed that AI hiring tools are biased against their age, race, gender, or background. Candidates also use AI, with 49.6% admitting they relied on it.
Ghost Listings
Some job postings never lead to hire, and workers call them ghost listings. Enhancv surveyed another 1,000 US professionals in March 2026. Among respondents with eight or more years of experience, 51% had encountered ghost listings, which are postings for roles the employer never intended to fill. Among 411 senior respondents, 31% said employers asked for strategy decks or marketing intelligence before making an offer.
Overall, 37% of respondents reported direct out-of-pocket losses. A job listing with no actual opening still costs applicants hours and money. In addition, 16.1% saw a role reposted as new right after a rejection email. Senior candidates who hand over strategy decks or marketing ideas before an offer may be giving away work for a job that doesn’t exist.
Who Is Overemployed and Why
Enhancv survey of 1,000 professionals with multiple full-time jobs also asked what it would take to give up the second paycheck. About half said they would need a 21% to 50% raise to give up the second paycheck. Another 12.9% said they would not leave, no matter the pay.
Enhancv’s data shows that overemployment spans office-based and hybrid roles across many industries. About 50.4% of respondents work mostly in the office and 26.5% work hybrid, so 76.9% have at least some on-site time. By industry, education leads at 16.6%, ahead of operations at 12.9% and healthcare at 11%. Software engineers account for just 2.3%, so most people hold multiple full-time jobs outside tech.
AI makes holding two jobs easier. In the same survey, 28% report a significant drop in workload from AI tools, and 8% said it fell by more than half. One in four meets primary targets in 30 hours or less. Roughly 26.4% rely on speed alone to keep multiple jobs running. Calendar blocking helps 15% of respondents, and 14.5% carry separate devices.
Employers Count Hours While AI Cuts Them
AI tools let workers finish tasks faster, but many employers still measure and reward hours worked. Many workers respond by adding a second job, so no single employer controls their income. Return-to-office mandates add to the distrust. An Enhancv return-to-office survey of 1,000 US employees found that 72% see the rules as a way to force resignations. Separately, 36% started a side hustle after their employer announced a return-to-work mandate.
Workers have learned that a job can disappear without warning, and that a rejection can arrive without reason. Enhancv’s research shows many now play around both.

articles.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.
AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.
But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.
“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan and Bank of America, the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eighth largest bank, changed its terms today.
Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tool leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account. Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.
As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector. But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.
Anthropic’s approach is telling: The personal finance tool it launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”
Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat. Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins. But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway. Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.
The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything from car-hailing to food service, and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.

articles.title: Nvidia’s rise, visualized
articles.text:
If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That’s how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change.
Nvidia’s rise, visualized
What’s next for Nvidia? Whatever doesn’t rock the mind-bogglingly profitable boat.
Nvidia’s rise, visualized
What’s next for Nvidia? Whatever doesn’t rock the mind-bogglingly profitable boat.
It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals, and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so?
But I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake.
It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you. I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now.
If you’re on a desktop OS, you could mouse over each dot in our chart above to see the staggering sums. But we built another way to visualize the rise of Nvidia I like even better. It’s a horizontal bar graph that not only puts Nvidia’s revenue growth in perspective, but shows you its monster profits right alongside them — plus the world events that made Nvidia a star.
TL;DR: The crypto boom and the great GPU shortage have nothing on the AI boom. Those earlier periods saw Nvidia’s profits briefly peak at $1.24 billion and $3 billion a quarter respectively, while the rise of data centers has driven them to $65 billion per quarter with no sign of stopping.
Yes, Jensen may have set a trillion dollars of Nvidia’s market cap on fire — from around $5 trillion at the start of November to “only” $3.6 trillion now — but the smoldering company is raking in $700 million in profit a day on average.
Put another way: Nvidia could give a $1 million bonus to every one of its 42,000 employees, every three months, without running out of cash. Or, you know, Nvidia could end world hunger or provide clean water for everyone, now that it’s making over $200 billion in pure profit a year.
Maybe that’d make people feel differently about data centers?
But even if we stick to self-serving capitalism, you’re probably still a happy investor if you bought Nvidia a decade ago. A $1,000 investment 10 years ago is now worth over $67,000. You’d have over $1 million if you invested $15,000 back then.
And make no mistake, Nvidia is sticking to capitalism. Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress just promised to return as much money to investors as possible on the company’s November 17th earnings call. “Going forward, we intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders,” she announced. “All” is a lot more than the 50 percent baseline that Jensen promised five months ago.
Nvidia isn’t the only company whose fortunes have risen this dramatically. RAMageddon revealed that just three companies — Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron — controlled nearly 90 percent of the entire global DRAM market, and those three have repeatedly signaled that they’d prefer to celebrate record profits instead of ramping up production too fast.
But while their revenues and profits have been skyrocketing even faster over the past year or so, even Big RAM hasn’t caught the AI wave quite the same way as Nvidia. Samsung, of course, doesn’t just make memory — its revenue numbers include phones, tablets, TVs, home appliances, chips, displays, camera sensors, audio, networking equipment, medical equipment, and more.
In the most recent quarter, Micron made $37.7 billion in profit, SK Hynix made $29.8 billion, and Samsung came in at around $55.3 billion, but they’re all shy of Nvidia’s $65.3 billion. Historically, RAM has also been a bit more cyclical: Both Micron and SK Hynix actually lost money in 2023 because they produced too much memory.
On its latest earnings call, the first since cofounder Jensen Huang’s resignation, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reinforced the idea that Nvidia expects the good times to keep on rolling.
Asked how things might change under new management, she suggested that they wouldn’t: “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual,” she said. She added that the company has secured the backing of customers and suppliers including TSMC, the all-important firm that actually fabricates Nvidia’s chips.
“Our momentum is real, our demand is accelerating, our supply is growing. Our customers and partners are with us, and employees are committed,” she claimed. “We’ve got this.”
Nvidia claims it’ll rake in even more money next quarter, with projected revenue of $130 billion. Profit may be proportionally smaller since gross margins are estimated to drop to 71–72 percent (compared to nearly 75 percent), but Kress said Nvidia intends to get them up as high as 73 percent next year.
In other words: This astounding gravy train isn’t going anywhere. At least that’s the plan.
Stevie Bonifield contributed to this story.

articles.title: Phố thời trang Hà Nội treo biển giảm giá 80% Black Friday, khách vắng hiu hắt
articles.text:
Dù còn hơn một tuần nữa mới đến Black Friday (27/11), nhiều cửa hàng thời trang trên các tuyến phố Chùa Bộc, Phạm Ngọc Thạch, Thái Hà (Hà Nội) đã đồng loạt treo biển giảm giá từ 50% đến 80%. Tuy nhiên, trái với những tấm băng rôn quảng cáo bắt mắt, lượng khách mua sắm vẫn khá thưa thớt.
Khảo sát trên phố Chùa Bộc cho thấy, nhiều cửa hàng quần áo, giày dép treo biển giảm giá 50%, 70%, thậm chí tới 80% ngay trước mặt tiền. Một số nơi còn bày thêm giá treo quần áo khuyến mại bên ngoài để thu hút khách.
Dù vậy, lượng người ra vào không nhiều. Phần lớn cửa hàng ghi nhận không khí mua bán khá trầm lắng.
Tại một cửa hàng thời trang nam quảng cáo giảm giá 50%, khách ghé vào chỉ đếm trên đầu ngón tay. Một số ít người xem qua các mẫu hàng rồi nhanh chóng rời đi. Một chuỗi cửa hàng thời trang nữ treo biển giảm tới 80% nhưng bên trong cũng chỉ có vài khách đang lựa đồ.
Tình trạng tương tự diễn ra trên phố Phạm Ngọc Thạch và Thái Hà. Các biển quảng cáo giảm giá xuất hiện dày đặc, song không khí mua sắm chưa sôi động. Nhiều cửa hàng chỉ lác đác khách ghé xem.
Khách hàng ngày càng thận trọng với khuyến mại
Không ít người tiêu dùng cho biết họ không còn quá hào hứng với Black Friday như trước. Trong bối cảnh phải cân đối chi tiêu, việc mua thêm quần áo, giày dép không còn là ưu tiên của nhiều gia đình.
Bên cạnh đó, trải nghiệm mua sắm trong các đợt giảm giá trước đây cũng khiến một bộ phận khách hàng dè dặt. Theo phản ánh của người mua, mức giảm sâu thường chỉ áp dụng cho một số sản phẩm tồn kho, mẫu cũ hoặc hạn chế về màu sắc, kích cỡ. Trong khi đó, các mẫu mới thường chỉ được giảm ở mức thấp hơn.
Chị Nguyễn Minh Trang (29 tuổi, nhân viên văn phòng tại Đống Đa) cho biết chị từng là "tín đồ" săn sale mỗi dịp Black Friday nhưng vài năm gần đây đã hoàn toàn đứng ngoài cuộc.
"Tôi không còn mặn mà với Black Friday vì nhiều cửa hàng treo biển giảm 70-80% nhưng thực chất chỉ áp dụng cho vài mẫu lỗi mốt, tồn kho từ mùa trước hoặc có chất lượng vải rất kém. Những mẫu mới, đẹp chỉ giảm tượng trưng 10-15%. Có nơi nâng giá gốc lên rồi mới hạ, tính ra chẳng rẻ hơn bình thường là bao", chị Trang nói.
Lê Hoàng Nam, sinh viên năm thứ ba Trường Đại học Thủy lợi, cũng cho rằng việc nhiều cửa hàng triển khai khuyến mại quanh năm khiến người mua không còn tâm lý phải chờ đến Black Friday mới mua sắm.
Theo Nam, với cùng một mẫu áo khoác hoặc đôi giày, mua trên sàn thương mại điện tử, kết hợp mã giảm giá và ưu đãi vận chuyển, đôi khi có thể tiết kiệm 20-30% so với mua trực tiếp tại cửa hàng.
Ở phía người bán, việc triển khai chương trình khuyến mại từ giữa tháng 11 được xem là cách thu hút khách, cải thiện doanh thu và giải phóng hàng tồn trước khi kết thúc năm.
Chị Linh, quản lý một cửa hàng thời trang, cho biết cửa hàng phải đẩy chương trình giảm giá sớm để kích cầu. Tuy nhiên, theo chị, lượng khách mua trực tiếp trong các đợt khuyến mại gần đây không đạt kỳ vọng.
Chị cho biết trong dịp Black Friday năm 2025, dù thương hiệu triển khai nhiều chương trình kích cầu từ giữa tháng 11, sức mua tại cửa hàng vẫn khá trầm lắng.
Theo người quản lý này, các cửa hàng thời trang đang chịu áp lực từ chi phí mặt bằng, nhân sự, đồng thời phải cạnh tranh với các sàn thương mại điện tử và hình thức bán hàng qua livestream.
Khi người tiêu dùng có thể dễ dàng so sánh giá, săn mã giảm và đặt hàng trực tuyến, lợi thế của việc mua sắm trực tiếp tại các tuyến phố thời trang giờ thu hẹp đáng kể.

articles.title: OpenAI says its AI found 14% gains in AMD's flagship GPU design
articles.text:
OpenAI says its models improved power, performance and area by up to 14% on AMD’s flagship GPU designs, with some changes in a chip sent for manufacturing and single-digit gains on AMD’s next flagship CPU. It also detailed AI-made gains on its own Jalapeño chip and is training a GPT-Synopsys model with Synopsys.
OpenAI says its AI models have improved the design of AMD’s flagship graphics chips, with some changes already in a chip sent for manufacturing. In a blog post on Wednesday, it reported gains of up to 14% in power, performance and area, the three measures chip designers trade off, against AMD’s heavily optimised designs.
The model rewrote the code that describes a chip’s circuits, and used Synopsys software to check each change still worked. OpenAI says this was about a year’s worth of progress in under five months. AMD also confirmed single-digit gains in key parts of its next flagship CPU, according to OpenAI.
OpenAI used the same approach on Jalapeño, its first in-house chip, which went from design to manufacturing in nine months. Changes suggested by its models cut the size of two key parts of the chip by about 13% and 10%, and worked in the finished silicon. Startups are chasing the same idea: Architect Labs raised $24M in June to help companies design custom chips with AI.
OpenAI also tested five generations of its models on designing two small open-source processors. Its newest, GPT-6.2 Astra, scored highest both when improving existing designs and when building a processor from written requirements. OpenAI noted the second test was easier, because models could leave out features the originals had.
Next, OpenAI is training GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys, which is refocusing on AI design, to run the design tools engineers already use. Not everyone is fully convinced yet. OpenAI’s own chip chief, Richard Ho, said last month he still does not fully trust AI design changes, so every one is checked.

articles.title: David Ellison says HBO will air critical Elon Musk documentary despite his $1B investment in Skydance | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Skydance CEO David Ellison says HBO will air Alex Gibney’s documentary about Elon Musk, even after news broke that the SpaceX founder had invested $1 billion in the newly formed company following its Warner Bro. Discovery and Paramount merger.
Following news of that investment, questions emerged over how Musk’s sizable stake in the company might affect Skydance’s plans to distribute a documentary that is highly critical of him.
When asked by The New York Times editor and columnist Andrew Ross Sorkin whether HBO would still distribute the documentary even with Musk’s stake in its parent company, Ellison said, “We have a pay-one deal with A24, who produced that movie. Of course, we’re going to honor the deal.”
He went on to say, “We believe in independence. We don’t believe in censorship of any kind.”
Co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz are tasked with bringing together two major streaming platforms, Paramount+ and HBO Max, along with a portfolio of networks, including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central, and Food Network, under a single corporate umbrella.

articles.title: Sony’s impressive Bravia 8 II OLED hits a new low price ahead of Black Friday
articles.text:
Black Friday is a great time to save on a new OLED television for your winter movie nights. Though, it turns out that you can already get a great deal on the 65-inch Sony Bravia 8 II, one of our favorite OLED televisions. It’s currently discounted by $1,100 at various retailers, including Amazon, Best Buy, and directly from Sony. That discount brings the price under $2,200, the lowest we’ve seen. You can also save $800 on the 55-inch model, which is typically $2,599.99 (Amazon, Best Buy, Sony), but now costs just under $1,800.
Sony’s impressive Bravia 8 II OLED hits a new low price ahead of Black Friday
This screen is one the best we’ve tested, and the lower price makes it more competitive with other OLED televisions.
Sony Bravia 8 II OLED TV
The Bravia 8 II was chosen as the “king of TV” by a panel of judges (including The Verge’s own Nilay Patel) in Value Electronics’ 2025 shootout. The OLED TV has excellent color accuracy, a bright panel, and a 120Hz refresh rate.
My colleague John Higgins praised the Bravia 8 II for its excellent image quality and engaging picture, though those positive traits are consistent with almost all OLED TVs. What sets this one apart is its impressive image processing, the bold colors from its quantum dot-equipped OLED panel, and that it looks great right out of the box (although he recommends using Professional mode). The screen was awarded the top spot at 2025’s Value Electronics TV Shootout, beating out similar offerings from competitors like Panasonic, LG, and Samsung.
For gaming, the panel can reach up to 120Hz at 4K, with both variable refresh rate and automatic low-latency mode to ensure that your content looks and feels good to play. The connectivity includes two HDMI 2.1 (one with eARC), and two HDMI 2.0 ports, giving you plenty of inputs for consoles and a Blu-ray player, among other gadgets. We spotted some color fringing of certain colors in dark scenes, and lamented the lack of a but it’s an otherwise excellent screen we can easily recommend.

articles.title: Doanh nghiệp áp lực phải trả hết nợ cũ để vay lãi suất thấp
articles.text:
Dù nhiều ngân hàng đã triển khai các gói tín dụng ưu đãi, giảm lãi suất cho vay 1,5-2%/năm, không ít doanh nghiệp vẫn khó tiếp cận nguồn vốn rẻ. Có đơn vị phải tất toán khoản vay cũ mới được vay với lãi suất thấp hơn.
Sau chỉ đạo của Chính phủ và Ngân hàng Nhà nước, mặt bằng lãi suất đã có sự điều chỉnh. Tuy nhiên, mức lãi suất công bố chưa đồng nghĩa mọi doanh nghiệp đều có thể tiếp cận vốn rẻ. Thực tế, một số đơn vị vẫn vướng điều kiện vay, hạn mức tín dụng và khả năng đáp ứng hồ sơ, khiến dòng vốn ưu đãi chưa đến được đúng lúc doanh nghiệp cần.
Phải tất toán khoản vay cũ mới được hạ lãi suất
Tại một doanh nghiệp kinh doanh thực phẩm ở Hà Tĩnh, ông H.M.C., Giám đốc điều hành, cho biết từ đầu tháng 11, các ngân hàng đã thông báo điều chỉnh giảm lãi suất đối với những khoản vay của công ty, mức giảm từ 1-1,4 điểm phần trăm. Trong đó, Vietcombank báo giảm lãi suất khoản vay trung hạn từ 8,6%/năm xuống còn 7,2%/năm, áp dụng trong một năm.
Tuy nhiên, để được áp dụng mức lãi suất thấp này, công ty ông phải dồn tiền để tất toán các khoản vay cũ, sau đó làm thủ tục vay mới cho một dự án thực tế.
Ông C. cho rằng nếu các doanh nghiệp không thu xếp được dòng tiền để tất toán nợ cũ thì khó có thể tiếp cận được vốn rẻ. Dù thời điểm này, mức lãi suất thấp hơn sẽ giúp doanh nghiệp giảm chi phí vốn, có thêm điều kiện chuẩn bị nguồn hàng phục vụ dịp Tết.
Trái với trường hợp trên, dù là đơn vị thuộc diện ưu tiên về vốn vay, ông Lâm Tuấn Ngọc, Giám đốc Hợp tác xã Nông nghiệp Tuấn Ngọc (TPHCM), cho hay khoản vay tại Agribank phục vụ mục đích xây dựng nhà lưới, nhà màng của đơn vị vẫn duy trì ở mức 9%/năm, cao hơn 1 điểm phần trăm so với thời điểm 2 tháng trước đó.
Ông Ngọc lý giải, muốn được hưởng lãi suất mới hợp tác xã phải tất toán khoản vay cũ và lập hồ sơ vay lại đúng mục đích. Tuy nhiên, hợp tác xã không có sẵn nguồn tiền mặt để trả ngay khoản nợ cũ, đồng thời hạng mục đầu tư đã hoàn thành nên không có cơ sở mục đích mới để tái vay.
Cũng theo vị này, với kinh nghiệm tài chính, ông cho rằng, việc điều chỉnh giảm lãi suất thường có độ trễ ít nhất 3 tháng kể từ khi có thông báo do nhà băng cần thời gian để lãi suất huy động đầu vào ổn định trở lại trước khi cân đối giảm lãi đầu ra.
Để ứng phó với lãi suất tăng, HTX Tuấn Ngọc buộc phải điều chỉnh tăng giá bán một số loại rau từ 10.000 lên 11.000 đồng/kg để bù đắp chi phí. Bên cạnh lãi vay, đơn vị này còn chịu tác động cộng hưởng từ chi phí nhiên liệu (xăng, điện, nước), tiền lương nhân công và chi phí tuân thủ tăng cao.
Tương tự, ở nhóm doanh nghiệp xuất khẩu gạo, ông Phạm Thái Bình, Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị Công ty Cổ phần Nông nghiệp Công nghệ cao Trung An, nhận xét, giữa định hướng chính sách và khâu thực thi tại các ngân hàng vẫn còn khoảng cách.
Cùng góc nhìn về áp lực vốn dịp cuối năm, ông Phan Văn Có, Giám đốc Marketing Công ty TNHH Vrice, chia sẻ, đặc thù ngành gạo là phải chuẩn bị nguồn hàng trước từ 2-3 tháng, thanh toán tiền mặt ngay cho nông dân và chịu chi phí lưu kho nên phụ thuộc lớn vào vốn ngân hàng.
Theo ông Có, lãi suất cho vay đối với Vrice tăng dần qua các tháng, từ khoảng 7,5%/năm trước tháng 9 lên 8,3%/năm vào tháng 11. Đây là mức áp dụng đối với doanh nghiệp chuyên xuất khẩu, có lịch sử tín dụng tốt và tài sản bảo đảm như bất động sản hoặc nguồn thu bằng ngoại tệ (USD).
Khi doanh nghiệp đề nghị ngân hàng xem xét giảm lãi suất, phía ngân hàng cho biết chi phí huy động vốn đầu vào vẫn ở mức cao nên chưa thể điều chỉnh ngay. Bên cạnh đó, hạn mức tín dụng dành cho doanh nghiệp còn hạn chế. Do vậy, nếu có nhu cầu vay vốn, Vrice phải chấp nhận mức lãi suất hiện hành và chờ ngân hàng cân đối nguồn vốn để giải ngân.
Trong bối cảnh cần nguồn tiền ngay để thu mua hàng tạm trữ cho các đơn hàng cuối năm và thanh toán các hợp đồng quốc tế, doanh nghiệp không thể chờ đợi 3-4 tháng để chính sách giảm lãi suất phát huy tác dụng. Đơn vị phải tự cân đối dòng tiền hiện có hoặc chấp nhận vay vốn ở mức lãi suất hiện tại để duy trì vòng quay kinh doanh, thậm chí chuẩn bị tâm thế lãi suất có thể tăng tiếp trong thời gian tới.
Vốn rẻ không có ý nghĩa nếu không thể tiếp cận
Theo các doanh nghiệp và chuyên gia, vấn đề khó tiếp cận vốn rẻ không hẳn nằm ở việc thiếu cơ chế, chính sách mà là khâu thực thi. Ông C. cho rằng những thông điệp về giảm lãi suất đã được đưa ra nhiều lần trên các phương tiện truyền thông, nhưng doanh nghiệp vẫn gặp khó khăn khi tiếp cận nguồn vốn phù hợp với khả năng sản xuất, kinh doanh.
Chủ tịch Hiệp hội Xuất nhập khẩu TPHCM Phạm Văn Xô bộc bạch, doanh nghiệp không nhất thiết đòi hỏi lãi suất quá thấp mà cần một mức hợp lý và ổn định trong thời gian đủ dài, bởi nếu lãi suất liên tục thay đổi, doanh nghiệp cũng không dám vay để đầu tư mở rộng sản xuất.
Dưới lăng kính kinh tế, TS Lê Bá Chí Nhân, chuyên gia kinh tế độc lập, nhận định, vấn đề lớn nhất của chính sách vốn rẻ hiện nay không ở việc ngân hàng có giảm lãi suất hay không, mà nằm ở chỗ dòng vốn này chưa thực sự đến được doanh nghiệp đang cần. Muốn vốn rẻ thực sự chảy vào nền kinh tế, ông Nhân cho rằng cần triển khai đồng bộ nhiều giải pháp.
Thứ nhất, chuyển trọng tâm từ giảm lãi suất danh nghĩa sang giảm chi phí vốn thực tế.
Thứ hai, thiết kế cơ chế giảm lãi suất đối với cả dư nợ hiện hữu. Những doanh nghiệp có phương án kinh doanh khả thi, lịch sử tín dụng tốt và không có nợ xấu cần được xem xét điều chỉnh lãi suất khoản vay cũ, thay vì buộc họ vay mới để được hưởng chính sách ưu đãi.
Thứ ba, thay đổi tư duy cấp tín dụng từ dựa chủ yếu vào tài sản bảo đảm sang đánh giá dòng tiền và năng lực tạo doanh thu. Rất nhiều doanh nghiệp có đơn hàng, thị trường và phương án kinh doanh tốt nhưng thiếu tài sản thế chấp. Đây chính là khu vực cần được khơi thông tín dụng.
Thứ tư, phát triển các quỹ bảo lãnh tín dụng, quỹ hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa, đồng thời mở rộng tín dụng theo chuỗi cung ứng.
Cuối cùng, phải phối hợp đồng bộ chính sách tiền tệ với chính sách tài khóa và cải cách môi trường kinh doanh. Khi sức mua yếu, đơn hàng thiếu và thủ tục đầu tư kéo dài, dù lãi suất thấp, doanh nghiệp cũng không dám vay.
“Vốn rẻ không có ý nghĩa nếu doanh nghiệp không tiếp cận được; tín dụng tăng trưởng cũng không đồng nghĩa với kinh tế tăng trưởng. Thước đo thành công của chính sách tiền tệ phải là số doanh nghiệp thực sự vay được vốn với chi phí hợp lý, mở rộng được sản xuất, tạo thêm việc làm và đóng góp vào tăng trưởng GDP, chứ không đơn thuần là mức lãi suất ngân hàng công bố”, TS Nhân nhấn mạnh.
Ông Nguyễn Đức Lệnh, Phó giám đốc Ngân hàng Nhà nước Khu vực 2, cho biết bên cạnh tín dụng ngân hàng truyền thống, cho thuê tài chính là một kênh vốn có thể hỗ trợ các doanh nghiệp hạn chế về năng lực tài chính.
Đến cuối tháng 9/2026, dư nợ cho thuê tài chính đạt khoảng 37.000 tỷ đồng, tăng trưởng 11,35%. Cho thuê tài chính tạo điều kiện cho các doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa đổi mới máy móc, đầu tư tài sản cố định và ứng dụng công nghệ hiện đại vào quy trình sản xuất.

articles.title: Sequel hits $26M in funding as it adds AI agents to on-site webinars
articles.text:
Sequel has raised $15M led by Sorenson Capital, taking its total to $26M. Its software runs webinars on a company’s own site and links what viewers do there, and it now sells AI agents that plan video programmes and turn talks into other content.
Sequel, a startup that runs webinars on a company’s own website rather than on a separate platform, has raised $15M, co-founder and CEO Oana Manolache wrote on Wednesday. Sorenson Capital led the round, with High Alpha, Album VC and Webflow Ventures joining. It takes Sequel’s total funding to $26M.
Manolache, who previously worked in marketing at HP, says standalone webinar tools send interested viewers away from a company’s site. Sequel keeps them there, and links what they watched and asked to what they did before and after.
It now sells AI agents built on that data. They can plan a video programme, turn one talk into other content and help turn viewers into sales leads. Customers can also plug in their own AI tools through an MCP server.
“Anyone can build an agent now. I can build one in five minutes in my spare time. But an agent without context is useless,” Manolache wrote.
Sequel says it has tripled revenue two years in a row and serves more than 400 companies, including ElevenLabs and Datadog. It did not share revenue figures or a valuation. It last raised an $8M Series A in 2022.
Its pitch leans on trust, as AI makes fakes easier to produce. Zoom has started letting users prove they are human on calls. Marketing tools are filling up with agents too: Adobe this month put its marketing agent inside ChatGPT and Claude, and Gradial raised $65M in June.

articles.title: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman believes that people should stay in charge of the future when it comes to how AI technology impacts the world and everyone’s lives. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the AI executive referred to discussions in Silicon Valley about whether there will be a gradual handover to AI — meaning AI will eventually become the decision-making authority across every major industry and institution.
“One thing we’ve been talking a lot about recently is there’s been this thing in Silicon Valley that seems almost ridiculous to have to fight against, but we both believe very deeply that people need to stay in control of the future, and there’s increasing talk about, well, there is either going to be or there should be this sort of gradual handover to AI. And I — we both — agree that that’s a terrible idea,” said Altman, who was sharing the stage with OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman.
The hand-off theory stems from the idea that as AI models become increasingly more powerful, they will learn to improve themselves — a concept known as “recursive self-improvement” or RSI. As existing AI technology builds newer, smarter generations, those will eventually become a superintelligence that humans can no longer control, the belief goes.
Altman explained that he and Brockman only disagree over how to best accomplish the goal of keeping humans in control, or what sort of challenges we should expect to face along the way. However, Altman characterized this as more of a debate between two people who share the same larger views.
“The question of how to actually prevent [handover] from happening — how to actually ensure that we will, given all of the various pressures and given what other companies may try to do — that we are going to actually ensure that people stay in control of the future in a very deep way, and we don’t have this either accidental or intentional handover — I think we can both agree on that,” Altman said.
Brockman added that, as the models improve, there’s an increasing responsibility for alignment, safety, and security, which may require changes in how things are currently done.
“Monitoring is a good example of something where I think we are going to need new … technology,” he said.
Today, AI researchers monitor the model’s chain of thought, where the AI writes out what it’s thinking as it works through problems and performs tasks. But in Brockman’s view, that may not always be the best way to monitor more advanced AI that’s being built now.
“As the models have gotten more capable, they can do more within just the forward path without having to actually write out that thinking, which means we need a new approach to monitoring,” Brockman said. “We’re going to need to deliver that, and I think that there will be points where we need to really think about, as the capabilities get to a certain point, chain-of-thought monitorability is degraded,” he continued, adding that all the problems were technical ones to be solved.
OpenAI had committed to increased chain-of-thought monitoring after the incident where an OpenAI model escaped containment and hacked into the AI model repository Hugging Face. In Wednesday’s interview, Brockman noted that the company told 25% of its production engineers to stop building things and work on securing the AI technology after the hack.
But despite the high-profile breach, he argued that forward progress was still critical to fight bad actors.
“I think to realize that if you look to the level of capabilities of models in the world, and you see cyber models that are coming from that are now … in the hands of threat actors everywhere, that I think that it’s really important that defenders use the most capable models to defend,” he said.

articles.title: Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
articles.text:
Instagram’s latest update will allow you to edit your Stories without losing your views, likes, or replies. You can now edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings for up to 15 minutes after sharing your Story, Instagram head Adam Mosseri has announced.
Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
You can edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings in your Stories for up to 15 minutes after sharing.
Reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi first spotted Instagram working on this feature in April, but now it’s official. Previously, you had to delete and repost your Story to fix a typo or add a song that you forgot to include.
You can edit your post by opening your Story and selecting the three-dot menu in the bottom-right corner. From there, tap “Edit Story” to start making changes.
In addition to editable Stories, Instagram announced that it’s launching new fonts, colors, and shapes for stickers, as well as presenting them on sticker sheets that are supposed to be easier to browse. The platform is also making changes to the way you select multiple photos and adding new blur, colors, and gradient background options.

articles.title: The leaked Lenovo Legion Go Beam could be the affordable handheld we need
articles.text:
For a while there, it seemed like Lenovo had given up on selling handheld gaming PCs, hiking the price of its Legion Go 2 and Legion Go S far higher than other RAM-starved competitors. A decent one can easily cost $1,000 if not $2,000 now. But it looks like Lenovo might be about to announce a relatively cheap handheld once again— the Legion Go Beam.
The leaked Lenovo Legion Go Beam could be the affordable handheld we need
It looks comparatively cheap — and that might be a good thing in this economy.
Windows Latest has leaked images of the handheld, and there’s no question it’s designed to be a value alternative to even the company’s least expensive Legion Go S variant. While it’s got the same big stippled grips and triggers for comfort, there’s only one USB-C port on the top instead of two, a comparatively cheap-looking D-pad, no touchpad, and only a single tiny intake and exhaust for its fan.
There’s no SteamOS logo where that would go, so it likely runs Windows instead… but then there’s that name, “Beam.” Perhaps you’ll “beam” your games to it because it’s a streaming and cloud gaming handheld, instead of one that primarily plays games on its own chip? Maybe that’s why it doesn’t need as much airflow as previous handhelds?
Perhaps there’s a partnership with Xbox Cloud Gaming specifically, and that’s why it’s all lit up in Xbox green?
But it might just be green because it looks nice with white, which has been the “value” color for handhelds so far (see: ROG Ally, Xbox Ally, and the Windows-based Legion Go S). And it might be “Beam” because there’s a literal beam of light on the bottom, even though the first thing I do with most handhelds is turn any and all distracting RGB lighting off. Or maybe it’s “Beam” just because it sounds like a friendly, fun, value-oriented name, instead of something “S” or “Pro.”
I won’t begin to speculate on the Legion Go Beam’s price, except to say that “cheap” may be relative. The Legion Go S was originally supposed to cost $499, but wound up costing far more except on the occasional sale. The Legion Go 2 was supposed to start at $1,099 but wound up costing $1,500 and up after RAMageddon. Streaming-first handhelds have been far cheaper, though, like the $249 Sony PlayStation Portal.
Lenovo has a history of announcing its new gaming devices at CES in January each year, including previous Legion Go handhelds, so I’m expecting to see an official announcement of the Lenovo Legion Go Beam then. Even if so, that doesn’t mean it’ll be available in January — there’s often a many-month lag.

articles.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says it's 'hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI industry is entering a new era, and not just because of its constant stream of new model releases and discoveries. The AI community must now push forward without one of its most influential figures, Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals involving affairs with two employees and an alleged Chinese spy, raising potentially far-reaching national security concerns.
Speaking onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman each revealed that they had spoken privately with Huang as the embattled former CEO’s public image continued to unravel.
“Jensen took one of the earliest big bets on us. We took a big bet on Nvidia,” Altman said. “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”
OpenAI has worked closely with Huang over the years. Nvidia invested $30 billion in the company earlier this year and designs the chips that power OpenAI’s technology.
Brockman added that he and his wife are friends with Huang’s family, so the couple had reached out “personally, just to be there for him and his family at this time.”
“I think it’s obviously a tough time for everyone, but again, I think Nvidia is such an incredible company,” Brockman said. “I think that… what Jensen has built there, it clearly is built to last, and so we’re excited to keep partnering and looking to the future.”
Huang’s impact on Nvidia and the broader AI industry has been so profound that nearly 200,000 people, including Elon Musk and other influential CEOs, have signed a petition calling for the chipmaker to reinstate him. Nvidia executives said during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday that they do not have plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return.
Altman was reticent to weigh in on Huang’s future at Nvidia. When asked whether he thought Huang could return, Altman replied, “One thing I did not appreciate was everybody on Earth speculating with some random theory.”
“I will say, I wish Jensen the best. I wish Nvidia the best,” Altman said. “I don’t think the world needs another set of random opinions on what’s going to happen here.”

articles.title: Science Corp raises $400m for its PRIMA vision implant
articles.text:
Science Corporation, a US brain-computer interface company, has raised $400m in a Series D round, it said in a blog post on Tuesday. The company has now raised more than $900m since it was founded in 2021.
Investors include Khosla Ventures, Tenet Healthcare, Y Combinator, 885 Capital, PLC Neurotech and the Ackman Oxman Institute, among others. Science did not name a lead investor or disclose its valuation.
The round comes eight months after Science raised a $230m Series C, which TechCrunch reportedvalued the company at $1.5bn.
Science is led by Max Hodak, a co-founder and former president of Neuralink. Its main product is PRIMA, a tiny chip implanted under the retina that works with a pair of camera glasses. It is designed for people who have lost central vision to geographic atrophy, a late stage of dry age-related macular degeneration.
PRIMA won a CE mark in July, allowing sales in 30 European countries. The company says it is the first brain-computer interface with a CE mark to restore form vision, meaning the ability to read letters, numbers and words.
Science said it will use the new money to make PRIMA available across more of Europe. It will also prepare for a US launch, seeking FDA approval through the Humanitarian Device Exemption route, a pathway for devices that treat small patient groups.
In addition, the funds will go towards research, manufacturing and the company’s biohybrid brain interface. That project uses lab-grown neurons to link electronics with the brain.

articles.title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
articles.text:
With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.
On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. Their immediate target was Roblox, which they accused of evading legal complaints about children allegedly groomed on the platform by enforcing its own forced arbitration clause against users who agreed to the terms as minors, in some cases even under the age of 10. Separately, a few blocks away, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Laurel Lee (R-FL) brought hotel heiress Paris Hilton to Capitol Hill to advocate for the Defiance Act, which would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators.
“The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors,” Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), who chairs the Judiciary subcommittee, told reporters after the Roblox hearing. “The more I see these companies evade regulations, the more I think there is nothing as powerful as a jury.” Hawley introduced a new bill with ranking member Dick Durbin (D-IL) to render arbitration agreements unenforceable for disputes over alleged child sexual exploitation or “child cyber injury,” which could include “reputational harm, mental suffering,” or death.
“The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors”
Roblox has sought to enforce its arbitration clause in lawsuits it’s facing over allegations that users were groomed on the gaming platform as minors, despite the company’s claims of protections. Roblox is facing about 180 lawsuits in a consolidated case over its alleged role in failing to protect children. Under the arbitration process, the public would not get to see legal discovery like the kind that’s come to light under recent cases against Meta. Hawley called the jury system “corruption-proof” and “an incredibly big hammer.”
Roblox has denied that it’s trying to dodge accountability. “Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” Roblox’s global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço said in a statement. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”
Congress has only a little more than three more weeks left in session before the end of the year, and a new Democratic majority will be sworn in come January. Republicans are expected to do their best to push through President Donald Trump’s nominees for judgeships and executive branch posts like FCC commissioner in the lame-duck session, as well as try to pass year-end bills like the National Defense Authorization Act, which often includes a range of other policy items. But some lawmakers are holding out hope that they can open up courthouses to new litigation over deepfake abuse and child predation.
Litigation has become one of the more successful ways for survivors of online harm to seek change. Congress has failed to pass many prominent child safety, privacy, and consumer protection bills, though it has begun to tackle the deepfake issue through the Take It Down Act. At the same time, attorneys general and individual plaintiffs have collected significant settlements and legal wins despite the broad scope of tech’s legal shield, Section 230. If bills like the Defiance Act or those seeking to end forced arbitration were to pass, tech companies and perpetrators of online harms could become vulnerable to a new wave of legal challenges.
“You will be amazed by how quickly the company will change its behavior once it is sued in public court”
In addition to Hawley and Durbin’s bill about forced arbitration, Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Katie Britt (R-AL), and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced a similar bill with a slightly different approach, including explicitly covering data privacy violations. At the Roblox hearing, Northwestern University law professor Myriam Gilles, an expert on forced arbitration, said she’s testified before Congress many times on this topic, but “never expected to come before this body to talk about its use against 9 year olds.” Passing either proposal, she said, would have a profound impact. “You will be amazed by how quickly the company will change its behavior once it is sued in public court.”
The Defiance Act would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators for damages, in an attempt to raise the cost of creating these kinds of images. Hilton visited Washington earlier this year to share how an intimate non-deepfake video of her at age 19 shared without her consent impacted her life, and she used her story to advocate for the Defiance Act. At Tuesday’s press conference, she said she would come back to Congress as many times as necessary for the bill to become law. “Some people might have thought that was the end of my fight,” Hilton said. “But when I make a promise to survivors, I keep it.”
Hilton said over 50 million people have been victimized by sexually explicit deepfakes. “For me personally, strangers have created over 100,000 AI-generated explicit images and videos portraying me in the most graphic and disturbing ways imaginable,” Hilton said. “If this can happen to someone with my resources and my platform, imagine how powerless a young girl might feel facing this completely alone.”
Hilton’s comments were followed by Elliston Berry, an advocate who said a classmate made an explicit deepfake image of her friend group “from an innocent social media post” when she was 14, and distributed it throughout her school. “In a matter of seconds, my sense of security disappeared,” she said. “For me, the Defiance Act means recognition that victims deserve to be heard, that their experience matters, and that their right to seek justice should not depend on how quickly technology advances.”

articles.title: Sony's updated turntable is an easy entry into the world of vinyl | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Record players and other retro tech are making a strong comeback, and I’ve recently rejoined the world of vinyl collecting. Lately, I’ve noticed myself turning to Spotify less frequently, so it felt like the perfect time to start using a record player again.
Choosing a turntable can be quite overwhelming, especially for beginners. That’s where Sony’s new PS-LX3BT turntable comes in.
Since 2019, Sony’s PS-LX310BT has been a go-to choice for vinyl newbies. Now that it has been discontinued, the PS-LX3BT emerges as its successor, keeping the same beginner-friendly approach while adding a few modern upgrades.
Currently priced at $399.99, the PS-LX3BT is designed for people who want to enjoy vinyl without getting too caught up in the technical side of things. It’s also a good option for those looking to upgrade from their first inexpensive turntable without having to learn how to set up or customize a more complicated audio system.
One of its biggest selling points is how easy it is to use. The PS-LX3BT features automatic playback, so you simply press start and the tonearm lifts, moves into position, and drops onto the first track for you. There’s no need to manually position the needle or worry about getting everything just right. It’s a small convenience, but one that makes the experience much less intimidating for newcomers.
Sony has also made a few welcome changes compared with its predecessor. The PS-LX3BT now uses USB-C for power and supports Qualcomm’s aptX Adaptive Bluetooth codec, allowing it to transmit audio at up to 24-bit/96kHz. It also has a traditional phono output alongside Bluetooth, so you can choose between a wired speaker setup and listening wirelessly.
One slightly strange design decision, however, is the repositioning of the start, stop, and tonearm buttons. On the older model, these were placed outside the dust cover. Now they’re underneath it, meaning you’ll have to lift the cover just to press start. It’s not a huge inconvenience, but still kind of annoying.
The turntable also offers USB connectivity for digitizing your vinyl collection. Connect it to a computer, and you can convert your records into digital audio files, which is useful if you want to preserve older records or listen to your collection on the go.
My biggest disappointment is the lack of a built-in speaker. It would have been nice to have everything included for someone just getting started. You’ll need to buy speakers (and possibly an amplifier) or compatible Bluetooth headphones separately, so keep that added cost in mind.
If you’re searching for a more affordable and beginner-friendly automatic record player, there are cheaper options, such as this $179 option from Audio-Technica. But overall, Sony’s PS-LX3BT is a solid choice for anyone ready to dive into the world of vinyl for the first time.

articles.title: Vero Security raises $11M seed to police AI agents at work
articles.text:
Vero Security has raised an $11M seed round led by TLV Partners for software that discovers the AI tools and agents employees use and enforces security policies as they run. It cites research showing most large companies give AI security to someone who already has another job.
Vero Security, a year-old startup that helps companies control the AI tools and agents their staff use, has raised an $11M seed round, it announced on Wednesday. TLV Partners led the round, with GTM Capital, Maple Capital and angel investors joining. Vero, based in New York and Tel Aviv, says several Fortune 500 companies already use it.
Its main product checks prompts and actions as AI agents run, and blocks those that break company rules. For example, it can stop a coding agent reading keys it has no need for, the kind of leaked tokens behind last month’s LiteLLM hack. Security teams set the policy, and Vero turns it into controls that update as AI tools change.
Vero is betting that few companies have staffed this job. Among firms with at least $10B in revenue, 65% have someone leading AI security, but only 18% made it a dedicated role, according to IANS and Artico Search. At the rest, it was added to an existing job.
“CISOs have seen enough dashboards and tables that tell their teams what’s wrong and leave the work to them,” said co-founder and CEO Elad Tessler.
Tessler previously led product at Astrix Security, which Cisco bought this year. Vero is also launching a free online course and community for AI security staff, which it says contains no sales material.
The field is crowded. Zenity raised $125M in August, Tel Aviv’s Bay raised $50M last week, and Pluto Security emerged with $42M in October. Security teams often cannot see the AI their companies use.

articles.title: Musk says Jensen Huang is irreplaceable, regrets midterm spending
articles.text:
Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team on a winning streak, while also expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterms.
"You've got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team," Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times' DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, "Doesn't seem like a smart decision to me."
Huang resigned last week following pressure after disclosing an affair with a woman who reportedly was suspected of being a Chinese spy, alongside reports of relationships with employees. He is expected to testify before the U.S. Congress next month around national-security and export-control issues.
The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously said it would be an "honor" to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang.
Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang's departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump.
"I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision," he said, adding, "We're not on the board, right?"
Musk and Huang have known each other for years through Nvidia's work with Tesla and OpenAI. Tesla has been a major Nvidia customer, while Huang has repeatedly praised Musk's AI strategy, including Tesla's self-driving work, xAI and the Optimus robot.
Midterms, Tesla and SpaceX
Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt "pretty foolish" about spending at least $474 million with little to show for it, though he added that "maybe it would have been much worse without that."
Musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House and Senate from all being controlled by one party. "If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money," he said.
In the same interview, he also appeared to distance himself from the MAGA movement. "I'm not MAGA," he said, adding that he wasn't sure what the term means.
On a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, Musk said areas of overlap now exist that "didn't exist before," pointing to AI, robotics and the AI software and chip-design teams at both companies.
He said any deal would require shareholder approval and "may or may not succeed." Musk added that he could not push through a transaction that was bad for shareholders because he would "obviously get sued."
Asked whether he should receive his Tesla pay award if a merger were completed, Musk said he should not be rewarded "just for doing a merger" and should receive stock-option awards only if Tesla meets its performance targets.
Musk also said SpaceX rents computing capacity to Anthropic under short-term agreements that either side can terminate, adding that the Claude AI chatbot-maker had expressed interest in an additional 10 gigawatts.
Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, raising $81.3 billion in what it said was the largest public offering on record, surpassing SpaceX.
Asked how he feels a year after describing his mind as "a storm," Musk said he feels "relatively at peace."

articles.title: Palo Alto stock surges as all signs point to how important cybersecurity is in the AI age
articles.text: Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday evening reported a beat-and-raise quarter, making clear that with the growing adoption of artificial intelligence comes even greater demand for an all-in-one platform solution to cybersecurity. The Club stock shot higher. Revenue in the company's fiscal 2027 first quarter increased 39% year over year to $3.45 billion, exceeding the Wall Street consensus estimate of $3.31 billion, according to LSEG. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) rose 13% to $1.05 in the quarter ended Oct. 31, ahead of the 97-cent LSEG consensus estimate. PANW YTD mountain Palo Alto Networks YTD Following the print, in after-hours trading, shares soared 9%, after a regular Wednesday session rally that saw the stock surge nearly 10%. In addition to strengthening demand alongside AI adoption, Palo Alto Networks announced an acquisition that should get the company even more deeply embedded with customers. It's not our discipline to chase huge rallies, so we're reiterating our hold-equivalent 2 rating. We are also keeping our price target at $400. Palo Alto has been volatile with some sharp ups and down since its record-high close of almost $420 on Oct. 6 Bottom line The need for all-encompassing, rapid-response cybersecurity platforms has never been greater. With every new AI advancement come more capabilities. It's a double-edged sword, however, because just as the good guys are getting more capable, so are the bad guys. While AI is helping the good guys identify vulnerabilities, the rush to patch them is causing its own issues. Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora described the lay of the land during an interview with Jim Cramer for "Mad Money" on Wednesday evening, using the numerous disruptions and outages recently happening across the nation to illustrate his points. "What has happened is that the Mythos moment about six months ago has become an inflection point for cybersecurity. You've seen, even in the last two weeks, that we've seen all these outages. We've seen some AI-assisted cyberattacks," he explained. "The pace of cyber activity is only going to increase. And what customers are realizing at this moment is that this approach that they had of spray-and-pray is not going to work. They're going to have to go consolidate into platforms." Platforms and scale are what Palo Alto and fellow Club name CrowdStrike specialize in. On the call, Arora said, "We believe many of the major disruptions over the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising the production environments. The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks. Bad actors are using open-weight models and new frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale." Looking ahead, Arora believes that the increased levels of security patches needed now that AI has become so advanced will continue for at least another 18 months – bringing with it the same risk of the collateral damage seen in recent weeks. That said, as time goes on, he believes, the risk will decrease as customers get smarter about how and when to patch, and update the ways in which they do so. Importantly, the CEO said that no patch will prevent the bad guys from trying to breach systems, stressing that every organization must expect and prepare for attacks. He added that the most important thing that must be done is to modernize the "north of $1 trillion of legacy security and IT infrastructure onto real-time platforms." As a shareholder, we recognize that the leading companies on the front lines of protecting computer systems stand to benefit greatly. It seems like AI has been around forever. But in reality, we're still in the early days of AI adoption, which means we have only just begun to see the cybersecurity risks it poses. Quarterly commentary Palo Alto's closely watched next-generation security annual recurring revenue (NGS ARR) increased 66% year-over-year in fiscal Q1, a sequential acceleration from the 63% growth rate in the prior quarter, which was itself an acceleration from the 60% in the quarter before that. The businesses included in NGS ARR are focused on subscriptions for its cloud-native services. This line item excludes hardware and legacy products. Net new NGS ARR more than doubled versus the year-ago period. Another key metric providing insight into the demand environment is net new platformizations , which came in at about 170 in the quarter; more than the previous two first-quarter reports combined, Arora said on the call. That represents a 2.5 times year-over-year increase. The CEO added, "Platformized customers now represent two-thirds of our next-generation security ARR, and continue to expand at a robust rate with net retention above 120%." Total remaining performance obligation (RPO), which represents business signed but not yet converted into revenue, increased 35% year over year, to $21 billion. That was also ahead of expectations. Acquisition details Along with the release, Palo Alto announced that it will acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion, in an all-stock transaction that is expected to close in the fiscal 2027 third quarter. Applied Compute helps with the post-training and inference phase of open-weight AI models. The acquisition stands to benefit Palo Alto in two ways. First, internally, it will help the team embed AI across its own security capabilities. Second, it will also allow Palo Alto to help its own customers implement their own secure, sovereign open-weight models. Open-weight models are those that allow the user to adjust the model's biases, versus closed models, such as those from Anthropic and OpenAI, where they control the behavior. On the call, Arora said, "We're already seeing the desire for sovereignty and control compel enterprises to adopt open-weight and open-source models, and early signs of that shift are clear, with open-weight models growing from under 5% of token traffic to more than 60% over the past year. … We expect a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars of enterprise applications driven by open-weight and open-source adoption. … These models must be delivered securely and, where required, in a sovereign fashion, with controls strictly in the hands of the enterprise. When we looked at training custom open-weight models ourselves, we looked for partners across the entire AI ecosystem looking for rare engineering rigor and a proven ability to address enterprise challenges. We landed on Applied Compute because no other team matched the technical pedigree in post-training open- weight models. We're now bringing a world-class team of frontier AI researchers in-house and expect to reach 100 researchers by year-end." Further speaking to the rationale of the deal, Arora said, "We have to get in the training business to be able to build a good supervision business. And that's our bet. … If it works, I think this will dwarf the abilities that we have in cybersecurity. This could be bigger than what we do today." The team expects Applied Compute to add over $1 billion of annual recurring revenue to Palo Alto's next-gen security ARR by fiscal 2029. To achieve this, Palo Alto will need to invest about $3 billion — or less than half a year of free cash flow — in one hundred-plus megawatts of compute capacity over the next three to five years. "Longer-term, we believe this is our next multi-billion-dollar ARR business and positions us to be at the frontier of AI security," CFO Dipak Golechha said. Despite the need for increased investments, Golechha added, "We intend to remain capital light, and will maintain strong free cash flow margins through and beyond the capex cycle." Fiscal 2027 Q2 guidance Revenue in Palo Alto's fiscal Q2 is expected in the range of $3.53 billion to $3.55 billion, above the consensus estimate of $3.42 billion, according to LSEG. Adjusted EPS is seen in the range of $1.01 to $1.03, which at the $1.02 midpoint beats the LSEG consensus estimate of $1.01 per share. Next-gen security ARR (NGS ARR) is projected to be between $10.2 billion and $10.22 billion, which is well above the FactSet consensus estimate of $9.91 billion. Remaining performance obligation (RPO) is expected to be in the range of $21.5 billion to $21.6 billion, which is above the consensus estimate of $21.49 billion. Fiscal 2027 guidance Total revenue for the company's full fiscal year is seen in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, well ahead of the $14.17 billion expected, according to LSEG. Adjusted EPS is expected to be between $4.26 and $4.30, ahead of the $4.18 LSEG consensus estimate, and up from the prior range of $4.16 to $4.19 per share. NGS ARR is projected to be between $11.48 billion and $11.53 billion, ahead of expectations of $11.13 billion, and up from the previous range of $11.075 to $11.175 billion. RPO is expected to be in the range of $25.3 billion to $25.5 billion versus estimates of $25.3 billion, and above the prior outlook of $25.2 billion to $25.4 billion.
