articles.title: Intel signs first external customer for advanced 18A chips
articles.text:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips.
"Resilient supply on the foundry is very important," Tan said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas. "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Tan added, without naming the debut client.
It's a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. After years of missteps and low yields, Intel touted 18A as key to a turnaround that would finally convert the company into a competitive chip manufacturer for non-Intel products.
"It's a huge win for foundry," Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview.
Pushkar Ranade, Intel's technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel's 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June. In May, reports indicated that Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel's foundry to make some of the chips for Apple devices.
Intel's stock has lost more than half its value since the end of September, with most of that plunge coming late last month after the company said revenue this quarter will be at least $1 billion shy of analysts' estimates due to a PC sales slump and supply chain challenges.
In considering who the customer may be, Bajarin pointed to Nvidia, Apple or the major hyperscalers that make their own custom processors.
"Amazon, Microsoft and Google are struggling to get capacity for their CPU ambitions at TSMC," he said. "So it makes sense that you go somewhere for at least some capacity."
Tan said in late October that he sees the global market for server processors increasing as much as five times over the next five years to about $200 billion, but that Intel can't currently meet customer demand.
Wall Street has turned on Intel of late after the chipmaker had become a top trade starting in the middle of last year. The U.S. government took a 10% stake in Intel in August 2025, and Nvidia followed with a $5 billion investment, as optimism grew around the prospect of U.S.-made chips that could replace an almost complete reliance on Taiwan.
Until now, Intel has had no marquee customer for its foundry business, primarily manufacturing chips for its own products at its factories, including a huge new campus in Arizona.
Intel is a leader in another step of the chipmaking process known as advanced packaging, where individual chips are packaged together and connected to the larger system. Tan also announced on Wednesday that Microsoft is its first publicly named customer for its most advanced packaging technology, known as EMIB.
—CNBC's Kif Leswing contributed to this report.

articles.title: One of the world's most contested seas is proving too much for Asia's leaders to resolve
articles.text:
One of the world's most contested bodies of water continues to cause problems for Asia's leaders.
A substantive Code of Conduct in the South China Sea does not seem to be feasible despite ASEAN nations expressing optimism that the negotiations could finally conclude after more than two decades, experts told CNBC.
The ASEAN summit in the Philippines failed to resolve it, despite Manila saying it intended to conclude the Code this year.
The crux of the issue is that China claims virtually all of the South China Sea as its own territory, despite international rulings saying it's not the case and historical claims from many other countries.
China's "nine-dash line" claim was ruled as invalid by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in 2016, although Beijing has refused to recognize that ruling.
Over decades, China has been building shoals into structures that strengthen its territorial assertions, and has become increasingly aggressive in policing the territory against nations such as the Philippines, that claim traditional rights over the maritime areas.
The Code of Conduct for the South China Sea aims to address areas where multiple ASEAN nations and China have disputes and competing claims.
Manila has reported that it had completed 80% of the negotiating text, with negotiations to continue under next ASEAN chair Singapore. But, experts are skeptical that a "substantive and effective" agreement can be realized, at least in the short term.
"It's an annual ritual. The ASEAN Chair commits to completing the Code of Conduct in January, but by November is reporting that — although great progress has been made — they didn't quite get there this year. Rinse, repeat," Ray Powell, executive director at gray-zone activities tracker SeaLight Foundation told CNBC.
He described the 80% number as "a meaningless statistic," given that the issue at hand was complex and contentious. 
ASEAN secretary general Kao Kim Hourn still sees potential for resolution. "I don't think it's a failure at all," he told CNBC's JP Ong. "There's still a lot of commitment and a lot of leadership on both sides to move ahead and get it done."
But Collin Koh, senior fellow at the Institute of Defence and Strategic Studies in Singapore's Nanyang Technological University, told CNBC that even if 80% of the text has been set, the 20% remaining contain the most persistent problems, including geographical scope, competing interests among ASEAN member states, and enforcement.
Koh said the original aim was ASEAN to negotiate with China "one-to-one," but, it has never been the case.
"It has always been 10 against one. Now you add Timor Leste. Now 11 against one. So, because of that, there is never any unified ASEAN position that they will bring to the table with with China," he pointed out.
Disputes in the South China Sea stretch at least as far back as the 1970s, with various countries such as Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam claiming various zones and islands in the critical maritime region, which houses rich natural resources and fishing areas.
'Unlikely to happen'
Back in 2015, Singapore has positioned itself as a "neutral broker" in ASEAN-China dialogue, with then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong saying that Singapore will deal "fairly and openly with all parties" in order to "preserve peace and stability in the region."
"China at its heart doesn't really want a code of conduct, and it continues to push more assertively into the South China Sea."Joshua KurlantzickSenior Fellow, Southeast Asia and South Asia, Council on Foreign Relations
But while the city-state may be able to broker some compromises, the disagreements that have held up the code for almost a quarter of a century will persist, according to Lynn Kuok, Lee Kuan Yew Chair of Southeast Asia Studies at the Brookings Institution.
"Beijing, moreover, has little incentive to accept meaningful restraints while it continues to consolidate its position in the South China Sea," Kuok added.
Her view was echoed by Joshua Kurlantzick, senior fellow for Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations, who said that a code of conduct is unlikely to happen soon, if ever. 
"China at its heart doesn't really want a code of conduct, and it continues to push more assertively into the South China Sea." He pointed out Beijing's actions against the Philippines in the region, including around the disputed Scarborough Shoal. 
Chinese coast guard vessels have most recently been accused of ramming Filipino fishing vessels near the Spratly islands in September, and have used lasers and water cannons against Filipino ships in the past.
Kurlantzick also said that there are multiple countries within ASEAN that are close to China that are willing to hold up any agreement on the Code, adding that the move toward China is also happening as the U.S.' commitment to defense in the region becomes less clear.
"I do not think there is really any chance of a code of conduct happening with Singapore as ASEAN chair — or really, anyone as ASEAN chair," he said.
At the same time, a rushed or flawed Code would be worse than none at all, Powell said.
"In fact, the worst outcome is not a failure to agree, but rather a weak Code that would enable Beijing to undermine UNCLOS," he said. The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which came into force in 1994, provides a comprehensive legal framework for oceans and seas globally.
"The narrative from China could then be 'see, now we have this shiny new regional agreement that overrides that problematic law invented by outsiders who don't understand East Asia and shouldn't have a say here anyway,'" Powell added.
—CNBC's Joanna Ossinger contributed to this article.

articles.title: Kash Patel skips House hearing after Mar-a-Lago gala with $50,000 access
articles.text:
After a string of outages disrupted airlines, banks and even the National Security Agency, U.S. House members gathered Wednesday to question the nation's top security officials. But FBI Director Kash Patel was nowhere to be seen.
The night before, Patel and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had been advertised as "honored guests" at the Big Blue Bash, a lavish charitable fundraiser at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago club, where attendees were offered access to a "private roundtable" and a stay at the venue for $50,000 a person.
Mullin appeared before lawmakers Wednesday morning at the committee's annual threat assessment hearing. Patel sent his deputy instead. And as the hearing got underway, a Justice Department jet that's been used by Patel before was still flying back from Florida.
Flight records reviewed by CNBC show the Justice Department aircraft associated with Patel's travel left West Palm Beach, Florida, at 7:51 a.m. Wednesday and landed at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington at 10:20 a.m. — 20 minutes after the House Homeland Security Committee hearing began.
The FBI confirmed Patel, Mullin and Attorney General Todd Blanche attended the Mar-a-Lago event.
"The event is approved by Ethics, following all guidelines and regulations," FBI spokesperson Benjamin Williamson told CNBC by email, noting the gala "is an annual event honoring fallen law enforcement officers and their families."
Patel's absence drew bipartisan criticism on Capitol Hill. Committee Chairman Andrew Garbarino, R-N.Y., said lawmakers had spent months trying to secure Patel's testimony, only for the FBI director to make clear he had "no intention" of appearing.
Rep. Bennie Thompson, of Mississippi, the committee's top Democrat, said Patel's absence for a second consecutive year undermined lawmakers' ability to conduct oversight. Prior to 2024, FBI directors traditionally testified at the annual hearing.
The episode also drew attention to what was being offered at Trump's private club: a chance for donors and corporate sponsors to meet privately with some of the nation's most powerful law enforcement officials.
"Trump's Big Blue Bash is yet another fundraising event that encourages wealthy special interests, particularly those seeking lucrative government contracts, to rub elbows with officials responsible for awarding those contracts," Craig Holman, a government ethics and lobbying expert at the watchdog group Public Citizen, told CNBC.
Billed as a tribute to federal officers and their families, the second annual black-tie gala came with a price list for access.
Gala tickets cost up to $50,000
General admission cost nearly $5,000, a VIP all-access pass $25,000 and a private roundtable with federal agency heads and a night at Trump's resort $50,000, according to the event's ticketing page. A sponsorship prospectus reviewed by CNBC advertised corporate packages reaching $1 million, including private briefings, speaking time and the chance to name and present an award to a federal agency of the sponsor's choosing.
Alongside Patel and Mullin, the advertised guest list also included White House border czar Tom Homan and leaders of Customs and Border Protection, the Secret Service, Drug Enforcement Administration and Transportation Security Administration.
It remains unclear which officials attended private meetings or which companies bought the most expensive packages. But several sponsors had substantial business with the agencies represented.
Motorola Solutions, the gala's top named sponsor, had approximately $237.1 million in fiscal 2026 net contract obligations from the Justice and Homeland Security departments, according to CNBC's analysis of federal records. That included a $139.6 million Bureau of Prisons radio contract, a $25.8 million Customs and Border Protection award and a nearly $18 million Secret Service contract option, all in September.
Motorola reported roughly $1.69 million in federal lobbying expenses this year through September, according to its first-quarter, second-quarter and third-quarter disclosures. Its lobbying included homeland security funding, communications technology and other issues.
"Motorola Solutions was proud to support last night's Big Blue Bash, honoring the families of wounded and fallen federal officers, whom we hosted as the night's guests of honor," the company said through a spokesperson. "We did not participate in private briefings."
Federal contractors supported gala
Two other federal contractors, the Vierra Group and Teya Diversified Services, sponsored a Department of Homeland Security presentation featuring Mullin and Homan, according to the gala's published program.
Federal contracting records show Teya received three Customs and Border Protection contracts in September worth approximately $23.3 million combined for repairs at northern border ports of entry. The awards included $9.1 million for work at 12 ports, $7.9 million for nine ports and $6.4 million for 10 ports.
LEO Technologies, which markets artificial intelligence and surveillance products to law enforcement agencies, was also listed as a sponsor.
Vierra, Teya and LEO Technologies didn't immediately respond to CNBC's requests for comment.
Ethics rules limit charitable involvement
Federal ethics rules require authorization for officials to participate in charitable fundraising in their official capacities and restrict the use of government titles for personal fundraising.
Holman said companies attending such events hope to gain favor with the administration and ultimately benefit through government contracts and policies affecting their businesses.
There is no evidence the sponsorships influenced federal contracts or secured preferential treatment, and some new contract awards added to existing contracts.
The financial questions extend to Trump's own business. Organizers haven't disclosed what Mar-a-Lago was paid or how much reached the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Foundation, the nonprofit that's the event's beneficiary. The gala offered a $1 million sponsorship package — more than the charity's entire 2024 revenue of $725,476, according to its latest available IRS filing — though no purchase has been confirmed. A Republican fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago cost about $318,000 in 2023, according to a New York Times analysis of campaign finance records.
The event also may raise questions about taxpayer-funded travel. Organizers listed Mullin as a speaker, and flight records reviewed by CNBC show a Gulfstream jet registered to DHS arriving in West Palm Beach Tuesday evening, alongside the Justice Department plane associated with Patel's travel. It remains unclear who was aboard either aircraft or whether the flights were connected to the gala.
Days earlier, Mullin used a government plane to attend a Louisiana State University football game shortly after a nationwide FAA ground stop. He defended the trip Wednesday to the House Homeland Security Committee, saying government travel was required and that he personally paid for it.

articles.title: Inside India newsletter: Foreign flows helped the market recover. Now it faces the inflation test
articles.text:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.
Welcome to the latest edition of "Inside India" — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.
As global portfolio managers look to diversify into non-artificial intelligence trades, India, with its strong economic growth and improved corporate earnings, is emerging as a top pick. But the country's inflation, which has been rising for 12 straight months, could impede inflows.
Any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team.
The big story
Foreign investors are returning to Indian equities in record numbers, but the country's accelerating inflation, which last month breached the central bank's comfort level for the first time in two years, could spoil the party.
India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, crossing the Reserve Bank of India's 6% upper limit, driven by surging food and transport costs.
Experts told CNBC that businesses have already started passing on increased costs to consumers, with signs of slowing demand visible in the rural economy and expected to hurt urban consumption by early next year.
"Rising inflation will squeeze household real incomes, while higher interest rates will weigh on investment and consumption, potentially putting pressure on corporate earnings," Alexandra Hermann Prasad, lead economist at Oxford Economics, told CNBC.
That could "temper foreign investor enthusiasm in the near term, even if India's structural growth prospects remain attractive," she added.
High-frequency indicators like car sales and credit card transactions softened in September while air passenger traffic declined for the fourth month in a row, Indian brokerage HDFC Securities said in a report on Tuesday.
As per data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations, released on Nov. 6, car sales fell 14.2% year on year in October. The industry body said that its "pressing concern is inventory" with dealers, which was elevated at 45 days in September and October, as against the usual range of 30 days.  
The inflation print "is not good," Gaura Sengupta, chief economist at India's IDFC First Bank, told CNBC, adding that inflation pressures led by supply-side shocks are spreading, and if that persists, it will affect corporate margins and household consumption.
She expects the RBI to raise benchmark rates by 25 basis points each over the next three monetary policies, taking the terminal interest rate to 6.25% by April next year.
The tightening of monetary policy is also likely to slow the recovery of the private investment cycle, denting India's economic outlook, experts said.
Growth worries
So far in November, foreign investors have pumped in more than $10 billion net in Indian equities. If that sustains, it will be the highest ever foreign capital inflow in a single month.
This would be a sharp contrast to earlier this year in March when foreign investors pulled a record $12 billion from India on worries that the energy shock from the Iran war could squeeze the economy and slow growth.
India's growth story, however, has remained intact so far, with corporate earnings showing a sharp improvement over the last two quarters. That resilience, alongside a rotation from AI names, has drawn investors back to India, as they look to diversify into non-artificial intelligence trades.
The fall in oil prices and the easing of tensions between Iran and the U.S. after the midterm poll results have also worked in India's favor, though experts warn that it is still too early to call November's rebound of foreign capital "a structural reversal."
"November's return of capital inflows primarily reflects lower oil prices, changing global risk sentiment following the US midterm elections, and growing concerns about the sustainability of the AI cycle, rather than a clear structural shift towards Indian assets," Hanna Luchnikava-Schorsch, head of Asia-Pacific Economics at S&P Global Market Intelligence, told CNBC.
That makes rising inflation a big worry for sustained inflows. Higher inflation could further weaken household demand, prompt monetary tightening, and slow earnings growth, making the return on Indian assets "less attractive," Luchnikava-Schorsch said.
India relies on imports to meet 85% of its crude needs and around 50% of its supplies transited through the Strait of Hormuz before the Iran war. Energy supply disruptions due to the Iran war have led to a sharp rise in inflation across several major economies in the world, including India.
"What matters more for attracting stable, long-term capital, and for weathering short-term swings in flows, is whether India can sustain the high growth path it is on," Madhavi Bokil, executive director, credit strategy & standards at Moody's Ratings, told CNBC, adding that higher inflation is a risk to that path.
Need to know
India's inflation crosses 6% in October after rising for 12 straight months
India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, crossing the Reserve Bank of India's 6% limit for the first time under the new series, owing to surging food prices. Inflation has been on the rise for 12 straight months in the South Asian country.
India raises export levies on diesel, aviation turbine fuel amid high inflation
India reportedly raised export levies on diesel and jet fuel on Monday, while keeping the duty on petrol exports unchanged. The increased levies on exports of key fuel items come on the back of rising inflation in India.
Coming up
Nov. 19: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO opens.
Nov.23: HSBC composite flash PMI for November.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Nvidia has a new problem — and it has nothing to do with earnings
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Wednesday that he sees another headwind for Nvidia following the abrupt resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang.
"You don't need to own Nvidia," the "Mad Money" host said. "Sure, the Interim CEO, Colette Kress, was brilliant on 'Mad Money' last night. The numbers weren't good; they were fabulous. But it doesn't matter. Because the market, like the tribe in Survivor, has voted Nvidia off the portfolio island."
Nvidia delivered blowout quarterly earnings Tuesday, with revenue more than doubling from a year earlier and guidance exceeding Wall Street's expectations. Complicating matters is Anthropic's blockbuster IPO, Cramer said, which is drawing investor enthusiasm further away from the chipmaker. Anthropic is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Thursday.
To illustrate the dynamic, Cramer compared the situation to visiting a favorite restaurant and being tempted by an exciting new special. Even if customers have ordered the same beloved dish for years, the prospect of something new can make them reconsider their usual choice.
In this case, Nvidia is the tried-and-true favorite, while Anthropic is the hot new offering. The AI startup's explosive growth and highly anticipated market debut are giving investors another way to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom, potentially reducing their appetite for Nvidia shares.
Cramer argued that the leadership uncertainty makes that decision easier. Despite Nvidia's impressive results and his praise for Kress, investors remain concerned about the company's future without Huang, the visionary founder who built it into the dominant supplier of AI chips.
"People want a company with a permanent CEO, and they want Jensen Huang," Cramer said. "They don't want to wait for Colette Kress and the board as they complete a search for a new one. ... They would rather just get some Anthropic."

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella calls Outlook outage a 'perfect storm.' Here's what went wrong
articles.text:
Microsoft could have done more to prevent the Outlook outage last week that brought swaths of corporate America to a standstill, CEO Satya Nadella acknowledged in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer.
"It was one of those crazy perfect storms where there was a latent bug that got sort of found only during a particular traffic pattern," Nadella said on "Mad Money" on Wednesday evening. "Of course, we should have done the testing before. We should have figured out how to have the bulkheads such that you didn't have a global outage."
The Outlook disruption last Thursday was the first domino to fall in a rough week for the technology sector, as a string of major outages disrupted everything from corporate communications to airline operations and banking transactions. The incidents underscored just how dependent everyday life has become on technology — and how indispensable Microsoft is to corporate America. That role is why its stock has long been a cornerstone of investors' technology exposure.
Nadella said the incident highlighted a broader challenge facing corporate America: as AI helps companies uncover software bugs faster, the growing number of updates needed to fix them can introduce instability into older systems.
"The thing that AI has done is it allowed us to find these bugs and fix these bugs. But that means you've got to then patch them, and that creates instability," he said, explaining that there's been an increase in how quickly companies develop, test and deploy fixes, known as "patch velocity." He added, "And I think a lot of what you're seeing is a little bit of, maybe, old infrastructure with new patches and instability."
Despite Microsoft's critical role in the business world, its stock had a rough start to the year as investors worried that advancements in artificial intelligence could upend seat-based software businesses. But the narrative started to shift over the summer, supported by Microsoft's strong cloud growth and relative spending discipline versus its hyperscaler peers.
Shares bottomed out for the year in late June, and since the company's late-July earnings report, the stock has climbed 30%. The momentum has stalled a bit of late, though. The stock has pulled back nearly 9% over the past two weeks since its all-time closing high on Nov. 4, the day after the midterm elections.
Nevertheless, Microsoft's latest earnings on Oct. 28 reinforced its business momentum. Azure cloud revenue surged 48% to $33.2 billion, highlighting robust demand for AI computing power. At its Ignite conference Tuesday, Microsoft also laid out its vision for Copilot as the central hub for workplace productivity, making the case that AI could strengthen its dominance in enterprise software rather than undermine it.
Copilot has faced criticism for lagging behind the AI offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI, in which Microsoft was an early investor. Nadella highlighted Microsoft's September overhaul of Copilot, which brought its AI tools into a single app and introduced consumption-based pricing for more advanced features. By charging customers for usage, Microsoft is helping to defend against a decline in the number of paid seat licenses, which had been at the heart of the AI disruption thesis earlier this year.
"So the consumption will go up, and people will have to have new business models. So, for example, in Dynamics now, a lot of our business is not about seats; it's usage," Nadella said. Dynamics is Microsoft's customer relationship management and enterprise resource planning application.
The Copilot update also reflected Microsoft's push to become less reliant on OpenAI's models in its own applications as their partnership evolves.
"You want Claude, you want OpenAI, or our own models? You can route across all of them," Nadella said.
Another one of the debates surrounding Microsoft and other cloud operators is whether their AI buildout plans will be derailed by growing opposition to data center construction. Some on Wall Street, including CNBC's Jim Cramer, argue that established tech giants like Microsoft stand to benefit, at the expense of smaller players such as the neoclouds.
Nadella acknowledged the challenge, emphasizing that companies must demonstrate the tangible benefits of their investments to the communities hosting their facilities.
"We have to win the hearts and minds and the votes one community at a time," Nadella said. "It's not about even a narrative that I can tell you, but it is about the reality that communities feel."
He pointed to Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft has operated a data center for roughly two decades, as an example of how such investments can benefit local economies through jobs, tax revenue and infrastructure improvements.
"The overall tax benefits that have come in have all gone to building a new school, a new city center, lots of the facilities that the people in the community love, and that and oh by the way the wages, the average wages of the people who are employed there is twice the average wage before," he said. "So we have created long term employment."
Nadella also addressed Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, which has dominated headlines from Silicon Valley to Wall Street and Washington. Microsoft is a big buyer of Nvidia chips for its Azure cloud.
"Jensen, let's face it, was a singular founder," he said. "He did a fantastic job building a great company. And by the way, I know [interim CEO Colette Kress]. She worked at Microsoft for a long time. She's a terrific person. Ian Buck, Nick Parker, who worked with us, who's there. So [these] are all fantastic people at Nvidia, and we are very thrilled to be partnering with the company Jensen built with the people that are at Nvidia. And then, of course, it's the Nvidia board will decide what happens next."

articles.text:
U.S. equity futures jumped on Wednesday night as investors looked ahead to Anthropic's public trading debut.
Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 125 points, or 0.3%. S&P 500 futures added 0.5%, and Nasdaq-100 futures surged 1%
Asia-Pacific markets were mostly lower Thursday. Japan's Nikkei 225 inched 0.54% higher, while the Topix fell 0.32%. South Korea's Kospi fell 1.5% as markets opened an hour later than usual due to the country's annual college entrance exam. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell 1.34%, while mainland China's CSI 300 was little changed. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 1.12%.
In Wednesday's regular U.S. trading, the blue-chip Dow lost more than 560 points, or 1.1%. The broad market S&P 500 fell 0.2%, marking its fifth consecutive losing session and longest slide since June. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%.
Traders are focused on how the company behind Claude performs when it debuts on the Nasdaq Thursday, trading under the ticker "ANT." The artificial intelligence company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC Wednesday.
Anthropic also upsized the offering, selling around 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
The market has become more cautious on AI as of late, with investors focusing on whether heavy spending on the build-out will translate into meaningful profits. The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) has fallen 11% this month, and embattled AI bellwether Nvidia has dropped 26% while the company grapples with the resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of neocloud CoreWeave, which had seen its bond yields trade above 16% earlier this month, is also down almost 13% in November alone.
"It'll be an important barometer for investors' AI appetite," Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said of Anthropic's IPO. "AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations."
"The challenge in that thesis is that hot IPOs rarely perform well right out of the gate, especially these days, when every company seems to be vying for a limited pool of capital to fund their AI strategy," she said. "While I wouldn't be surprised to see the stock market take cues from Anthropic's performance, I'd caution investors about trying to read the tea leaves from one event too much."
On Thursday, traders will keep an eye out for weekly jobless claims. On the earnings front, Walmart is slated to report in the morning, followed by clothing retailer Gap after the market close.

articles.title: Palo Alto inks $4.5 billion deal for AI startup Applied Compute, shares pop 7% on earnings
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks shares jumped more than 7% after the cybersecurity firm beat Wall Street's fiscal first-quarter estimates and inked a deal for artificial intelligence startup Applied Compute.
Here's how the company did versus LSEG estimates:
- Earnings per share: $1.05 adjusted vs. 97 cents expected
- Revenue: $3.44 billion vs $3.31 billion expected
Revenue jumped 39% from $2.47 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Fears of AI-powered cyberattacks, heightened by incidents like the Hugging Face breach, are driving demand for cybersecurity vendors like Palo Alto Networks. Amid this backdrop, the company's shares have jumped 85% this year.
"As AI reshapes the threat landscape, we must continually evolve to protect our customers and enable them to adopt AI securely," CEO Nikesh Arora said in a release.
Palo Alto said annual recurring revenue for its next-generation security business jumped 66% from a year ago to $9.73 billion. Arora said the NGS ARR was one of the highest beats in the company's history.
The cybersecurity company bumped up guidance for fiscal year 2027 as businesses spend more on security in the age of AI.
Palo Alto expects adjusted earnings per share in the range of $4.26 to $4.30 and revenue in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion. The forecasts topped the earnings of $4.18 per share and $14.16 billion in revenue expected by analysts.
Net income totaled $482 million, or 57 cents per share, up from $334 million, or 47 cents per share, a year ago.
Palo Alto Networks has been steadily acquiring companies to capitalize on demand for cyber tools in the age of AI.
Arora said the company's $4.5 billion all-stock deal for Applied Compute will help businesses secure open-weight models as adoption grows. The startup helps businesses run and customize their own AI models and marks a major investment for Palo Alto beyond cybersecurity.
"If it works, I think this will dwarf the ability that we have in cybersecurity," Arora said on an earnings call. "This could be bigger than what we do."
Outages from Microsoft, banks and air traffic control have heightened concerns around cyberattacks over the last week. U.S. officials have so far ruled out any malicious activity, but experts say the rapid acceleration in patching is straining dated systems.
As businesses discover more vulnerabilities, Arora said the company expects tens of thousands of virtual patches by the end of the fiscal year. 
"Whatever they do today is going to take three to six months, maybe nine months, depending on how complex and how tired their environment is," Arora said.

articles.title: CEO turned informant: How the FDA built a case against executives promising cheap medications
articles.text:
The federal case against an alleged illegal prescription drug operation and its two top leaders earlier this month features a notable informant: the CEO of a peer company that authorities say was committing the same import violations.
John Thomas Howard, treasurer and director of a Canadian healthcare company called CANARX, was arrested in the tunnel connecting Detroit and Canada on Nov. 8 and charged with smuggling, conspiracy and importing a misbranded drug for patient use in the United States. His brother and the president of the company, Bob Howard, is wanted on similar charges and was still being sought as of last week, according to court records.
The charges mark the first criminal case by U.S. authorities against a company that's part of a cottage industry known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, that promise to lower or eliminate high prescription drug costs for Americans.
The cheaper medications are typically sourced from international markets, a business model that the Food and Drug Administration and Department of Homeland Security say is illegal and can put patients' health at risk.
At issue is the unregulated nature of drugs intended for foreign markets and, in some cases, the risk of counterfeit products. And while AFPs generally argue that the importation of medication is allowable under U.S. law by individuals for personal use, authorities contend the operations go too far.
CANARX, based in Windsor, Ontario, was established in 2002 and was featured in a CNBC investigation into the booming AFP industry.
Joseph Morris, general counsel for CANARX, told CNBC last year that the business was operating legally and was confident in the safety of the prescriptions it provided. Last week, Morris told CNBC that the Howard brothers "deny all the charges against them, will defend vigorously, and expect to be vindicated in court."
CEO turned informant
The FDA's case against CANARX started with a tip about a similar healthcare operation called ScriptSourcing. It is detailed in a 35-page affidavit — dated Oct. 29 and unsealed last week — written by Dustin Dobbs, special agent with the FDA's Office of Criminal Investigations.
Based in Bonita Springs, Florida, ScriptSourcing marketed its international prescription program to self-funded employer health plans. Founder and CEO Gary Becker was described on the company's website as a "health insurance and risk management consultant for more than 30 years."
ScriptSourcing had been on the FDA's radar since at least 2022 for potential drug import violations, according to the affidavit. In August 2025, Dobbs, posing as someone interested in the AFP business, emailed ScriptSourcing and asked if the company was FDA-compliant.
A ScriptSourcing employee in responses to Dobbs said the company was FDA-compliant and that it had more than 2,000 name brand specialty medications and worked with more than 3,000 self-funded health plans.
However, that same year, the agency learned of two alleged incidents in which medications from ScriptSourcing's international drug import program had harmed patients, according to Dobbs' affidavit. One patient had been hospitalized due to a small bowel obstruction after she used misbranded Mounjaro sourced by the company via a Canadian pharmacy, and another was allegedly seriously injured after receiving a counterfeit medication.
Facing scrutiny from the FDA, ScriptSourcing CEO Becker turned on the Howard brothers of CANARX.
By May 2026, Becker had become a cooperating witness for the government in its investigation into the Canadian firm, Dobbs wrote. Becker told the FDA that he had done business with CANARX on drug importation and that the company had given him a "road map" on how to operate, according to the affidavit.
ScriptSourcing provided the FDA with a spreadsheet of financial transactions with CANARX between 2021 and 2026. It showed approximately 16,549 prescription drugs have been dispensed, the affidavit said.
Then, in several recorded phone calls between June and July 2026, Becker discussed the foreign importations with the Howard brothers.
The phone calls "show that John Howard was aware of the routes for importation of drugs from Canada into the United States and has tried to mold them to fit [CANARX's] illegal drug importation program," Dobbs wrote in the affidavit. "These phone calls also show that John Howard and Bob Howard were aware that these drugs were not allowed to enter into the United States legally."
Among the shipments en route or being prepared by CANARX at the time the information was provided was a package that contained Neupro, an FDA-regulated drug for the treatment of Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome.
The FDA did not respond to a request for comment from CNBC on the details in the affidavit.
Gary Becker's attorney, George Karavetsos, declined to comment when reached by CNBC, but confirmed on Monday that ScriptSourcing was no longer in business.
AFPs' position
The AFP business model was at the center of a civil lawsuit originally filed by Gilead Sciences in December 2024 that alleged several companies, including CANARX, illegally imported its HIV drug Biktarvy. CANARX has not responded to Gilead's allegations.
Gilead said in a statement to CNBC last week in response to charges against the Howard brothers that it "welcomed the government's efforts to hold accountable those whose conduct may put patients at risk."
"Pharmaceuticals manufactured for foreign markets are almost always considered unapproved and misbranded drugs under U.S. law, whether counterfeit or even if made by the same manufacturer that produced the version sold in the United States," Dobbs wrote in his affidavit.
— CNBC's Melissa Lee and Paige Tortorelli contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nvidia's shift in financing tone may spell trouble for Coreweave, other neoclouds
articles.text: Coreweave and other neoclouds were slumping Wednesday as investors anticipated tighter financing from Nvidia — one of the industry's biggest backers under former CEO Jensen Huang. While the stocks popped in after-hours trading following the big Nvidia earnings call on Tuesday, the gains proved short-lived. CoreWeave and Iren were down around 3% in afternoon trading, though Nebius bucked the trend, trading up around 2%. This segment of cloud computing companies is at the forefront of the physical AI buildout. It's distinct from the big, established hyperscalers like Microsoft , Amazon.com , Meta Platforms and Alphabet . The necoulds, which rent out AI compute and cloud capacity, may deliver big returns for investors if they succeed. But some have racked up large debt loads and will need additional financing to build and equip planned data centers. They're also risky due to the special types of financing and guarantees they require to fulfill their AI-focused objective. During the Nvidia call, analysts picked up on a subtle shift in Nvidia's tone on financing that could suggest difficulties ahead for the neoclouds. Interim CEO Colette Kress touched on the need for "discipline" with regard both to the neoclouds and the capital allocation strategy on which some of them rely. "The company indicated they would continue with their plans, but showed small signs that they may be scaling back their ambitions," Jay Goldberg, senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners, said in a Wednesday note. "In particular, they changed language in their financial footnotes to emphasize that data center delays would lead to cancellation of their financial Commitments." NVDA 1M mountain Nvidia one-month chart Bernstein analyst Stacey Rasgon also picked up on the footnote change. "There looks to be a new sentence, a new paragraph on the neoclouds. It says your commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products … It says certain commitments may be reduced or eliminated if they don't do this," he said during Nvidia's earnings call. Kress responded that the passage in question indicated Nvidia's position on the specific timing of the guarantees under consideration and that contractual obligations would stem from there. "What we are indicating in our statement there is, that is when our guarantee starts," Kress said, adding that Nvidia guarantees wouldn't remain in place in the event of construction delays. Morgan Stanley credit analyst Lindsay Tyler said in part that Nvidia's report "left the ecosystem support trajectory opaque," according to a Wednesday note. Kress reinforced an emphasis on counterparty selectivity, powered shells and prepayments, Tyler noted. But Tyler added, "the future scale remains unclear." Tyler kept her forecast for Nvidia's "debt adjustments and contingent obligations unchanged" at around $170 billion by the end of 2028. And she retained her revenue sharing/price floor framework for chip and equipment financing. But she now forecasts 4 gigawatts of deployment, down from 5 gigawatts, due to disclosed neocloud commitments declining to $32 billion from $36 billion quarter-over-quarter. Nvidia may also have different capital allocation priorities now, she added. "Strong top-line and guidance reinforce core fundamentals, but greater share buyback ambitions and supplier-funding needs temper our previous cash accumulation," she said. Further complicating the story for the neoclouds are signals from the Federal Reserve that additional interest rate increases may be needed to quell inflation, which would make financing more expensive, putting pressure on some heavily indebted neoclouds. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that a half-percentage point increase at the December meeting may be necessary .

articles.title: Why Anthropic's hot IPO is bringing out sellers — plus, a silver lining of the down market
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Stocks are struggling to mount a sustained rally despite Nvidia's strong earnings, upbeat forecast, and positive revision of its cloud industry backlog. As we said earlier , Nvidia's report had something for both the bulls and bears. While the guidance was impressive and the stock is historically cheap on an earnings basis, the quarter didn't change Jim Cramer's view that investors should take some shares off the table, if they haven't already, as a matter of capital preservation . A down session for the S & P 500 would be its fourth straight and would extend the pullback from its all-time closing high to more than 6%. That's still pretty far from a correction, defined as a decline of at least 10% from recent highs. For the week, the S & P 500 has dropped about 3%. Some of the pressure over the past few days may be tied to a bit of selling by investors making last-minute room for their Anthropic allocations ahead of Wednesday night's initial public offering (IPO) pricing and Thursday's first trade. These types of moves tend to happen around IPOs as the market absorbs the new supply. A silver lining to the bearish sentiment and continued selling pressure is that this could be the push needed to get the S & P Short Range Oscillator into oversold territory. We have kept our powder dry, waiting for this signal to get more opportunistic and begin deploying our 16% cash position. An attempt at a midday rebound fizzled . The timing of the move coincided with a pretty quick drop in oil prices. West Texas Intermediate crude traded slightly above $84 per barrel around 11 a.m. ET, but fell to around $82.50 about an hour later. This quick drop in WTI, the American oil benchmark, brought down Treasury yields despite Federal Reserve Christoper Waller's call on Wednesday to "shock people" with a half-point interest rate hike. We often point out the linkage between oil prices and the stock market because energy costs affect so many parts of the economy, including inflation expectations, input costs, and consumers' discretionary spending. While stocks were unable to maintain their lift, the drop in oil and bond yields stuck. Palo Alto Networks reports quarterly results after the bell and CEO Nikesh Arora will be on "Mad Money," fresh off the earnings call. On Tuesday, Arora posted on X about all the tech outages lately: "What the industry tried to warn enterprises about 6 months ago is here. The events of this week so far are not a coincidence. AI is making it easy for hackers to attack multiple customers," he said. Club stock Palo Alto rose more than 8%. On Thursday morning, we'll get earnings from Walmart , Alibaba, and Bath & Body Works. It's a quiet day for economic data, with just the Philadelphia Fed's business outlook and the government's weekly jobless claims scheduled before the bell. articles.title: Nvidia interim CEO Kress tells employees ‘let’s move forward’ at first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang exit
articles.text:
Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress told employees "let's move forward" on Wednesday during the company's first all-hands meeting since founder Jensen Huang resigned, a person who attended the meeting told CNBC. The person asked not to be named because the meeting was private.
Kress was joined by newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones and hyperscale and high-performance computing head Ian Buck.
Several other senior members of Nvidia's executive team spoke or joined Kress on stage, including longtime company veteran Jeff Fisher, senior vice president of software engineering Dwight Diercks, senior vice president of GPU engineering Jonah Alben, executive vice president in charge of operations Debora Shoquist and co-founder Chris Malachowsky, according to people familiar with the matter.
Kress opened with the message about moving forward and also mentioned pay raises and explained that the yearly review process, when employees typically get pay raises and are granted more stock, would be moved up from March to December. Nvidia shares are down 37% from their 52-week high.
Jones discussed the search for the next CEO, the person who attended the meeting said. The meeting lasted about an hour and was in person as well as streamed on Microsoft Teams.
The general sentiment swirling in the room, according to the person, was that employees want Huang to come back. Employees have spoken up on X in recent days to call for the return of Huang as CEO, and one senior employee reportedly sent a letter to the board warning Nvidia would lose "irreplaceable talent" if it doesn't consider reinstating Huang.
But another person familiar with the matter disagreed, saying that employees welcomed the remarks from leadership as well as the visibility into company leadership. The person asked not to be named because the matter is private.
"The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said during the company's earnings call on Tuesday.
Some executives shared that they do not agree with Jones. "Why make such a strong definitive statement when the investigation is still playing out," an employee told CNBC. The employee asked not to be named given the sensitivity of the subject.
The meeting was held one day after Huang said he was ready to return as CEO should the board want him. Multiple employees told CNBC that Huang's letter "fired employees up."
Despite recent turmoil, Wednesday's meeting was not out of the ordinary. Nvidia typically holds all-hands the morning after quarterly earnings reports, according to a former employee, who asked not to be named because the matter is private. Kress recapped Tuesday's earnings report, calling it a "great quarter," according to the person who said employees welcomed the remarks and visibility from leadership.
In past meetings, Huang took time to answer questions submitted by employees, according to the former employee. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the executives also answered pre-submitted questions in Wednesday's all-hands.
Nvidia shares were down Wednesday, a day after the company reported third-quarter earnings that topped Wall Street expectations and gave no signal that the company was going to slow its growth.
Correction: This story has been revised to reflect that executives at Nvidia's all-hands meeting answered employee questions. A previous version mischaracterized how executives handled employee questions.

articles.title: Nvidia's earnings report had something for the bulls, bears and everyone in between
articles.text: Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang's resignation last week had something for everybody — the defiant bulls, the invigorated bears, and anyone in between. For us, we saw enough encouraging signs to stay with the embattled stock, especially the chipmaker's plans to spend its money going forward. The most obvious positive in Tuesday night's report was Nvidia raising its revenue growth target for the fiscal year starting in February to 75% from 70% . Some of the skeptics argue that they still don't know how much of Nvidia's sales into Southeast Asia have been driven by Chinese-linked demand, as the U.S. government tightens export controls to the region in the wake of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. There are other details from the quarter that can be spun multiple ways. Take gross margins. Yes, Nvidia is seeing pressure from higher memory prices and the ramp of its Vera Rubin generation server racks, resulting in guidance for the current quarter between 71% and 72%, and for next fiscal year in the range of 72% to 73%. Both targets are below the 75% ballpark that Nvidia investors have grown accustomed to during the AI boom. At the same time, these marks are still well above the mid-50% range seen at its closest competitor, fellow Club name Advanced Micro Devices . Plus, interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress emphasized that efforts to secure more supply chain capacity drove their ability to raise revenue guidance. That may be a direct result of getting additional memory supply, underscoring the advantages of being the dominant AI chip designer. That doesn't change overnight, with or without the visionary Huang as CEO. Shares of Nvidia fell 2% on Wednesday, as its pop at the opening bell quickly fizzled out. As we get more distance from the results, conference call, and Jim Cramer's exclusive interview Tuesday night with Kress , we remain committed to holding Nvidia shares through this period of turbulence. Yet we're not oblivious to the challenges ahead and uncertainties at hand, so we continue to believe investors sitting on big gains should book some profits if they haven't done so already. What Kress had to say Tuesday night — both on the post-earnings conference call and to Jim on "Mad Money" — about how Nvidia will spend its AI windfall was a clear-cut positive. It starts with that monster stock buyback and extends to its financial support for the larger artificial intelligence ecosystem. Buyback Nvidia repurchased $22 billion worth of stock in the three months ended in October, a new quarterly record. But it's a record that will be short-lived. Kress said Nvidia ended the quarter with $227 billion remaining on its buyback authorization, and that the company plans to complete the program by the end of its fiscal 2028 (that is the company's fiscal year beginning in February). Nvidia in September added $150 billion to its prior buyback authorization, in a move we cheered at the time because Jim had been pushing the company to be more aggressive in this department. There are five quarters between now and the end of its fiscal 2028, as Nvidia is currently roughly a month into its fiscal 2027 fourth quarter. To exhaust its $227 billion in remaining buyback firepower within its stated timeline, Nvidia would have to repurchase an average of $45.4 billion per quarter. That's simple back-of-the-envelope math, and in reality there would likely be quarter-to-quarter variation in the amount spent on buybacks. But using that simple average illustrates our point: Nvidia will spend a lot more money on buybacks in the coming quarters than what we've seen in the past. This will help support earnings growth and demonstrate management's long-term confidence in the business. With the stock's recent pullback and undemanding valuation of 10 times next 12 months' earnings estimates , we wouldn't be surprised to see a lot of that firepower deployed soon. Guarantees and investments Another positive: Kress struck a more disciplined tone about how Nvidia will lend support to other AI companies. This gets to the heart of the debate around "circular deals" and "vendor financing," which had intensified this year as Nvidia offered more backstops and credit guarantees to neoclouds and AI startups, and struck strategic partnerships with companies in its supply chain. Huang was seen as the driving force behind this ecosystem investment, which had led Nvidia to be dubbed "the central bank of AI." While signaling that Nvidia is not walking away from supporting the ecosystem, Kress said the company offered more details on the structure of its guarantees for its customers' data center projects. In her CFO commentary released alongside earnings, Kress wrote: We have partnered with leading neoclouds to enable broader access to our AI infrastructure to serve AI startups, model builders, enterprises, research organizations and sovereign customers. Our commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us. The language around when the commitments take effect is what's new. On the earnings call, Kress said this doesn't represent a change in Nvidia's strategy, but rather a change in how the company is communicating the strategy to Wall Street. Nvidia disclosed that it had $118 billion in guarantees at the end of the quarter, up from $108.5 billion previously. The vast majority — $105 billion — is related to the sprawling Softbank-OpenAI data center project in Ohio. In her interview with Jim, Kress said Nvidia's "our guarantees have been thoughtfully completed to date," and speaking more generally, she said the company's investments into the AI ecosystem haven't been done carelessly. "There's a lot of discussion internally with a lot of the teams on what we think are the best ones that we want to do," she told Jim. "And we're going to continue down that path to make sure we choose the right investments for us to work through going forward." Overhangs So why is Nvidia stock down Wednesday if the numbers were so strong and the company offered these additional positives on putting its financial might to work? With all the moving parts in the Nvidia story right now, you cannot pin it on a single factor because there is no one overhang. Some people could be raising funds ahead of Anthropic's initial public offering, which is expected to price Wednesday night, before the stock begins trading Thursday. The mounting scrutiny and investigations in Washington aren't helping things, either. On Tuesday afternoon, The Wall Street Journal reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the company. On Wednesday, Republican Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina confirmed to CNBC that Huang agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee. Also, Nvidia's delayed 10-Q filing may be creating a shroud of uncertainty that is keeping buyers on the sidelines. Public companies must file this quarterly financial statement with the SEC 40 or 45 days after the end of their quarters. In recent years, Nvidia's 10-Qs have been filed the day of its earnings press release, so Kress saying the company plans to file it "in the coming weeks" is a deviation. However, the uncertainty about who will be Nvidia's next full-time CEO — and specifically the chatter about the potential for it to be Huang himself — may be the biggest obstacle for the stock right now. Jim made this case on Wednesday's Morning Meeting, arguing, "I think Jensen is causing a lot of this weakness." In a statement Tuesday, Huang said he'd be open to returning as CEO if the board determined it was in everyone's best interest. It came after a petition supporting his return racked up signatures, and President Donald Trump even said he "would not mind" if that happened. Despite this, Board Chair Harvey Jones pushed back that evening near the start of Nvidia's call, declaring that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Kress reiterated that message in her interview with Jim. Jim said on the Morning Meeting that as long as there's this public back-and-forth over a potential Huang return, it will be tough for the stock to find a bottom. articles.title: Đúng sáng nay - 19/11, một máy bay đặc biệt dài 44,5m, sải cánh 35,8 m chuẩn bị vượt biển hơn 5 giờ để tới Việt Nam, hạ cánh sân bay Nội Bài
articles.text:
Đúng sáng nay - 19/11, một máy bay đặc biệt dài 44,5m, sải cánh 35,8 m chuẩn bị vượt biển hơn 5 giờ để tới Việt Nam, hạ cánh sân bay Nội Bài
Chiếc máy bay này có gì mà lại được gọi là máy bay đặc biệt?
Sáng 19/11/2026, một chiếc máy bay mang số đăng ký VN-A932 được thông báo chuẩn bị cất cánh từ sân bay quốc tế I Gusti Ngurah Rai trên đảo Bali (Indonesia), bắt đầu hành trình vượt biển kéo dài hơn 5 giờ để tới Việt Nam. Theo kế hoạch, điểm đến của chiếc máy bay là Cảng hàng không quốc tế Nội Bài, Hà Nội.
Thông tin được hãng hàng không Sun PhuQuoc Airways đồng thời đăng tải. Nội dung từ hãng cho biết, đây chính là thành viên mới trong đội bay, nâng con số tàu bay lên 24. Việc đưa thêm máy bay mới về Việt Nam trong tháng 11 nhằm phục vụ kế hoạch mở rộng quy mô hoạt động của hãng.
Qua hình ảnh được công bố, chiếc VN-A932 nổi bật với phần thân màu trắng, dòng chữ SPA cỡ lớn cùng phần đuôi phối các gam đỏ, cam và vàng đặc trưng của Sun PhuQuoc Airways. Máy bay có thiết kế thân hẹp với hai động cơ phản lực đặt dưới cánh, mang đặc trưng của dòng Airbus A321.
Dòng máy bay dài 44,5 m, sải cánh gần 36 m có gì đặc biệt?
Theo thông tin từ nhà sản xuất Airbus, dòng máy bay A321neo có chiều dài thân 44,51 m, sải cánh 35,8 m và chiều cao khoảng 11,76 m. A321neo thuộc gia đình A320neo của Airbus, được thiết kế với cấu trúc thân hẹp, một lối đi giữa hai dãy ghế. Dòng máy bay này có thể phục vụ các đường bay nội địa và quốc tế, với sức chứa tối đa 244 hành khách tùy cấu hình được lựa chọn.
Một trong những đặc điểm nổi bật là thiết kế đầu cánh Sharklet, giúp cải thiện hiệu quả khí động học, giảm lực cản trong quá trình bay và góp phần tiết kiệm nhiên liệu.
Theo Airbus, việc kết hợp thế hệ động cơ mới với các cải tiến khí động học cho phép A321neo giảm khoảng 20% lượng nhiên liệu tiêu thụ và phát thải CO₂ trên mỗi ghế so với thế hệ máy bay trước trong các điều kiện so sánh do nhà sản xuất công bố.
Bên cạnh đó, dòng máy bay này còn sở hữu khoang hành khách được cải tiến nhằm nâng cao sự thoải mái trên các hành trình dài. Thiết kế thân máy bay tương đối lớn trong nhóm tàu bay một lối đi cũng giúp các hãng hàng không linh hoạt bố trí số lượng ghế phù hợp với nhu cầu khai thác.
Đáng chú ý, các biến thể thuộc gia đình A321neo có thể phục vụ những hành trình quốc tế tầm trung và xa hơn. Trong đó, phiên bản A321LR được thiết kế cho tầm bay lên tới 7.400 km, tùy điều kiện khai thác.
Chỉ 10 ngày trước vừa đón máy bay thứ 23, hướng tới đội bay 33 chiếc vào cuối năm
Việc đưa VN-A932 về Việt Nam diễn ra chỉ 10 ngày sau khi Sun PhuQuoc Airways tiếp nhận chiếc máy bay thứ 23. Cụ thể, theo thông tin do hãng công bố ngày 9/11/2026, chiếc Airbus A321NX mang số đăng ký VN-A930 đã hạ cánh xuống sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài lúc 15h20, sau hành trình hơn 2.000 hải lý từ Bali (Indonesia).
Đây cũng máy bay thuộc thế hệ Airbus A321neo, có tuổi đời khoảng 1,5 năm tại thời điểm tiếp nhận. Cả VN-A930 và VN-A932 (máy bay thứ 23 và 24) đều được hãng thông báo thực hiện hành trình từ Bali về Nội Bài.
Trước đó nữa, ngày 21/9/2026, Sun PhuQuoc Airways cũng chính thức tiếp nhận chiếc máy bay thứ 20, Airbus A321LR mang số đăng ký VN-A926. Chỉ một ngày sau, hãng tiếp tục đón chiếc Airbus A330 thân rộng đầu tiên, mang số đăng ký VN-A969, tại Cảng hàng không quốc tế Phú Quốc.
Theo thông tin trên website chính thức của Sun PhuQuoc Airways, việc bổ sung dòng A330 giúp hãng mở rộng năng lực khai thác những đường bay quốc tế dài, bên cạnh đội bay A320/A321 phục vụ các hành trình nội địa và khu vực.
Trong thông báo ngày 10/11/2026 về thỏa thuận mua động cơ với CFM International, Sun PhuQuoc Airways cho biết hãng đặt mục tiêu nâng quy mô đội bay lên 33 chiếc vào cuối năm 2026 và khoảng 100 chiếc vào năm 2030.
Theo kế hoạch, đội bay mở rộng sẽ tạo nền tảng để hãng phát triển thêm mạng đường bay, tăng khả năng kết nối Phú Quốc với các thị trường quốc tế.
Đối với hành khách, việc gia tăng số lượng máy bay có thể tạo điều kiện để các hãng hàng không bổ sung chuyến bay, nâng tần suất khai thác và mở thêm lựa chọn lịch trình. Tuy nhiên, các máy bay mới cần hoàn tất những thủ tục kỹ thuật, pháp lý cần thiết trước khi tham gia khai thác thương mại.
Việc tiếp tục bổ sung máy bay cũng diễn ra trong bối cảnh nhu cầu đi lại, du lịch được dự báo gia tăng vào dịp cuối năm 2026 và Tết Nguyên đán 2027. Đồng thời, Phú Quốc đang chuẩn bị hạ tầng hàng không và du lịch để phục vụ các hoạt động trong khuôn khổ APEC 2027.

articles.title: Fed officials expect more rate hikes, worry about AI impact on inflation, minutes show
articles.text:
Federal Reserve officials expressed confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to stem inflation, though they decided to hold off while gathering more information, according to meeting minutes released Wednesday.
Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk."
More broadly, officials said "inflation pressures in the economy were broad based" and would warrant action, with "some" policymakers advocating for a quarter percentage point hike at the meeting. A couple of participants even noted the possibility that a larger increase might be needed at the next policy meeting in December.
The meeting summary said "almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate … would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective."
In a CNBC interview Wednesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller reiterated his belief that the Federal Open Market Committee should consider a half-point hike in December.
AI concern
Officials at the meeting expressed a high level of concern over AI, both as a source of inflation and financial instability.
Fed staff members who briefed participants noted "that off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint."
"Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," the minutes said. "A few participants remarked that AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms."
Officials said they still expect inflation to fall off sharply in 2027 and beyond as the impact from the current shocks wear off.
Ultimately, the FOMC voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark overnight borrowing rate locked in a range between 3.75%-4%. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase.
Those voting in favor of the hold "pointed to benefits in accumulating additional information, which would help in determining the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal."
Since the meeting, the inflation data has shown that the pace of price increases remains well above target.
The consumer price index in October rose 0.4% for all items and 0.3% for the core that excludes food and energy. Both readings were 0.1 percentage point higher than expected.
While indicating concern over how stubborn inflation has been, most Fed officials who have spoken publicly advocated a patient approach.
Potential 'shock' to markets
However, Waller said Wednesday that the Fed may have to "shock" markets by approving a half-point hike in December. He is the only central banker to espouse that belief publicly, though St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said he anticipates as much as a full percentage point move higher by the spring of 2027. As governor, Waller is a permanent FOMC voter; Musalem will not vote until 2028.
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Friday on CNBC that the central bank risks losing its credibility if it doesn't act.
At the core of policymakers' concern is whether rising prices related to the Iran war and President Donald Trump's tariffs, in many cases temporary events that wouldn't prompt a response, are instead becoming more entrenched.
Markets are fully pricing in a quarter percentage point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting that includes low odds of a half-point move, according to the CME Group's FedWatch gauge. Futures traders also are pricing a solid likelihood of two more increases in 2027.

articles.title: Đoạn clip khiến Ninh Dương Lan Ngọc phải ra mặt bênh vực Quốc Anh
articles.text:
Đoạn clip khiến Ninh Dương Lan Ngọc phải ra mặt bênh vực Quốc Anh
Ninh Dương Lan Ngọc giải thích câu chuyện đằng sau và bảo vệ bạn diễn Quốc Anh trước những chỉ trích.
- 08-11-2026Phim điện ảnh đầu tay cán mốc 100 tỷ đồng, hoa khôi SN 1999 tiết lộ chuyện hậu trường với Ninh Dương Lan Ngọc, Quốc Anh
- 27-10-2026Việt Nam có gia đình doanh nhân giàu có với 2 con trai đều là thạc sĩ Anh Quốc: Anh sinh năm 1989 là Phó Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị ngân hàng, em sinh năm 1995 làm Chủ tịch hãng hàng không
- 24-10-2026Quốc Anh lần đầu đóng cảnh nóng
Mới đây, một khoảnh khắc hậu trường tưởng chừng chỉ mang tính vui đùa lại bất ngờ khiến Quốc Anh trở thành tâm điểm tranh luận trên mạng xã hội.
Cụ thể, đoạn clip được ghi lại trong quá trình ghi hình Chị Chị Em Em 3. Khi phát hiện có một con ếch, Ninh Dương Lan Ngọc tỏ ra hoảng loạn vì vốn sợ loài vật này. Biết rõ nỗi sợ của bạn diễn, Quốc Anh đã ôm chặt cô, tiếp tục trêu chọc khiến nữ diễn viên cố gắng vùng vẫy, mếu máo. Khoảnh khắc này sau đó được chia sẻ rộng rãi trên mạng xã hội và nhanh chóng thu hút sự chú ý.
Tuy nhiên, phản ứng của khán giả lại chia thành nhiều luồng ý kiến. Một bộ phận cho rằng Quốc Anh có hành động đùa giỡn thiếu tinh tế, cử chỉ động chạm quá thân mật và không phù hợp với giới hạn giữa hai diễn viên. Một số bình luận còn bày tỏ sự khó chịu khi thấy Lan Ngọc liên tục vùng vẫy trong lúc bị bạn diễn giữ chặt.
Ở chiều ngược lại, cũng có người cho rằng đây chỉ là khoảnh khắc vui đùa giữa hai đồng nghiệp vốn đã thân thiết sau thời gian dài làm việc chung. Dù vậy, tranh luận vẫn tiếp tục lan rộng, đến mức phía ekip đã gỡ đoạn clip khỏi các nền tảng chia sẻ.
Giữa lúc Quốc Anh nhận về nhiều ý kiến chỉ trích, động thái của Ninh Dương Lan Ngọc càng khiến câu chuyện được quan tâm. Chiều 18/11, nữ diễn viên đăng tải hình ảnh chụp chung với bạn diễn, đồng thời lên tiếng giải thích về tình huống trong clip. Theo Lan Ngọc, thời điểm ghi hình trời mưa, mặt sàn sân ướt và trơn trượt. Bản thân cô trước đó đã bị trượt chân ngã một lần.
Nữ diễn viên cho biết Quốc Anh thực tế đã nhắc cô về sự xuất hiện của hai con ếch. Tuy nhiên, do không nhìn thấy chúng nên Lan Ngọc vẫn chưa hình dung được tình huống. Đến khi bất ngờ phát hiện con vật ngay trước mắt, cô mới giật mình và hoảng loạn.
"Lúc diễn cảnh này là mưa ướt nhẹp sàn trơn khúc sân bà Liễu đi ra té u mông 1 lần. Mà tội cậu có nhắc 2 bà ếch đó rồi mà nhìn hoài không thấy tới lúc thấy là bấn hồn nên cậu cũng sợ chạy té thiệt. Giai đoạn này là thân nên cũng hiểu nhau rồi. Cậu trên phim thấy đẹp trai chứ ngoài nhát mà lành lắm. Cảm ơn cậu cùng phối hợp với cô Liễu trong chuyến hành trình này nha", Lan Ngọc viết.
Cả hai có dịp làm việc cùng nhau trong Chị Chị Em Em 3, bộ phim đánh dấu sự trở lại màn ảnh rộng của Lan Ngọc sau khoảng 4 năm. Trong phim, nữ diễn viên đảm nhận vai Thị Liễu, còn Quốc Anh vào vai Văn Tài. Hai nhân vật có mối tình nhiều ngang trái, bị cuốn vào mối quan hệ tình cảm ngoài luồng giữa những ràng buộc về hôn nhân và danh phận.
Trong các hoạt động quảng bá phim, họ cũng thường xuyên có những màn tung hứng tự nhiên, tạo cảm giác thoải mái khi đứng cạnh nhau. Không chỉ phối hợp trong những cảnh quay tình cảm trên màn ảnh, cả hai còn có nhiều khoảnh khắc hậu trường vui vẻ. Quốc Anh từng chia sẻ anh hồi hộp khi lần đầu thực hiện những phân cảnh thân mật táo bạo với Lan Ngọc. Nam diễn viên cho biết bản thân chủ động xin phép bạn diễn trước mỗi cảnh quay để mọi người cảm thấy thoải mái hơn. Anh cũng gửi lời cảm ơn đàn chị vì đã hỗ trợ mình hoàn thành vai diễn.

articles.title: Stocks to watch as U.S. tech outages put "digital resilience" in focus
articles.text: A wave of disruptions across the U.S. is giving investors a reason to consider stocks in the business of "digital resilience." A string of outages affecting businesses and government agencies has shaken confidence in America's digital infrastructure. A highly classified communications network used by the National Security Agency went down on Tuesday, according to CNN and other news outlets. That followed a Microsoft outage on Nov. 12 and 13 , a Federal Aviation Administration ground stoppage, and outages at companies including JPMorgan Chase , United Airlines , Apple , and Marriott International . The disruptions have various causes, but they highlight the need for "digital resilience," a broad category spanning the gamut from data backup to securing communication networks. There's also an investment angle, as Bespoke Investment Group pointed out on Tuesday. The firm identified a basket of 29 digital-resilience stocks in the S & P 1500, including areas like backup and recovery, content delivery and traffic routing, monitoring and incident response, multi-cloud infrastructure, data-center power, government IT contractors and cybersecurity. "Companies increasingly need to keep data, websites, applications and essential services running when a system or network fails," Bespoke said in its note. While many of the stocks could benefit from a push for digital security, the group's performance has varied widely over the past month due to idiosyncratic factors. A10 Networks, which provides network security and application delivery tools, rose 25%, while IT services provide, Kyndryl gained nearly 21%. ServiceNow , a workplace software company, fell 35.9% and monitoring software provider Datadog dropped 32%, the steepest declines. Here's Bespoke's list and their one month performance. Valuations also diverge sharply. The cheapest stocks on Bespoke's list include government contractors Booz Allen Hamilton , Leidos and Parsons , all trading below 1.0 times price/sales over the next 12 months. Cybersecurity stocks, not surprisingly, are priciest; CrowdStrike tops the list at 32.2 times sales followed by Palo Alto Networks at 17.5 times. Also on the pricier side is Datadog at 11.6 times sales. Other players in the space Blake Anderson, director of portfolio management at Carson Group, told CNBC that he expects GoDaddy , Akamai and Cloudflare to be among the strongest players in the space. Their performance relative to software and semiconductor stocks, he said, may reflect investors' view that these companies are becoming more important. "Truth be told, 'digital resilience' is almost expected from every major technology provider nowadays," he said. Jeff Weniger, chief investment strategist at Corgi Invest, told CNBC that cybersecurity stocks could benefit as businesses respond to new digital threats. "Investors are transitioning from direct AI plays to those that capitalize on AI's second- and third-order effects," he said. In France, hackers accessed supermarket refrigeration systems and raised temperatures in hundreds of stores and in a separate attack, hackers used a fake job interview to compromise a Binance employee's computer before stealing $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency, "Cybersecurity firms can help prevent that type of thing by monitoring for malware and/or unauthorized script behavior," Weniger said. Despite their pricey multiples, shares of Crowdstrike were up 8% and Palo Alto was up 7% in Wednesday treading. The Amplify Cybersecurity ETF was also barreling ahead, up 5%.

articles.title: Nvidia reverses, metals crash ahead of Anthropic IPO
articles.text:
Is this what it takes to clear room for $1.5 trillion of new supply?
Slumping crypto prices, a big Nvidia reversal despite good earnings, and now a sharp drop-off in metals prices from gold to copper — cross-asset selling has traders wondering if Anthropic's incoming IPO is spurring a rotation trade with the aim of freeing up cash to buy stock in the AI giant when it goes public on Thursday.
Shares of Nvidia swung from $164 overnight to below $152 during Wednesday's trading session despite smashing analysts' expectations on revenue and guidance. Options volume on the stock was almost three times the average and showed a bullish bias despite the reversal, with almost twice as many calls trading versus puts, Cboe LiveVol data show.
Meanwhile, metals prices fell across the board, led by a 5% sell-off in copper futures to the lowest since April. Gold futures lost more than 3% to $3,744, the lowest since September 2025, despite Treasury yields slipping on the session.
Almost 300,000 options traded on the SPDR GLD Shares ETF (GLD), with a slight bias towards calls. The catch for gold bugs is that more calls looked like they were initiated by sellers, according to Cboe LiveVol data, which show 52,000 calls sold on the bid versus 45,000 calls bought on the ask.
